12.2 21+ for adult-use HDCPs (45:190): label "This product is intended for use by adults 21 years and older. Keep out of reach of children"; retail sale to adults 21+ for adult-use list (delta-8, delta-10, THCA, THCV, HHC, THCP, THCM, delta-6 — Run 1); products sold behind counter with ISO COA (Run 1); regulation distinguishes adult-use from other cannabinoid products; whether non-intoxicating CBD has any Kentucky minimum age not stated in text opened [VERIFY — do not impose 21+ on all CBD by analogy] Corrected https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kentucky/902-KAR-45-190 ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/902/045/190/14787/ Resolved: 902 KAR 45:190 provides (a) only non-intoxicating and cosmetic cannabinoid products may be sold to persons under 21; (b) all adult-use products shall be secured in the retail setting to prevent theft or other access to persons under 21, and shall not be sold, gifted, or otherwise transferred to any person under 21; (c) a retail seller of adult-use products shall require proof of age verifying 21+; and (d) adult-use products may be delivered/shipped to consumers over 21 in packages clearly marked "Adult-use only". The "secured" wording replaces the looser "behind the counter" paraphrase (behind-counter is a practical description, not the regulation's word). Non-intoxicating CBD therefore has NO 21+ floor in this regulation. See G12-09 (age limb resolved).
12.2 CIBs: 21+ (Run 1, SB 202 / ABC) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/902/045/190/14787/ As written (Run 1 finding, carried; no contradiction found).
12.2 Medical vaporising products: 21+ for purchase (1:070 — shall not sell vaporising-intended products to cardholder under 21 or to caregiver for patient under 21; Run 1); patients under 18 only with parent/legal-guardian designated caregiver (KRS 218B.025(2)); persons under 18 may not enter/remain on cannabis-business premises (KRS 218B.095(2)(c)) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/070/ As written. The 1:070 21+ vaporising rule is confirmed in the current LRC text.
12.2 Web/social access: businesses' websites/social media shall use measures ensuring accessors of allowable content are 18+ (1:090 §2(6)); 18 (web) vs 21 (purchase/vaping/HDCP) distinction — do not merge Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/070/ As written.
12.3 No per se THC limit in Kentucky law as opened; Kentucky has not adopted 5 ng/mL (or any ng/mL) per se THC limit; 2025 proposal HB 34 (2025) would have amended KRS 189A.010 to create per se marijuana-concentration offence (secondary summaries describe 5 ng/mL in one version and 6 ng/mL in jacketed bill text for SB 230 / BR 1897) — did not become law (BillTrack50: HB 34 introduced 7 Jan 2025, to Judiciary (H) 4 Feb 2025, dead 28 Mar 2025 as indexed); do not quote 5 or 6 ng/mL as law Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/25RS/sb230/orig_bill.pdf As written, clarified: the 6 ng/mL text is in the jacketed SB 230 / BR 1897 bill text (proposed subsection (1)(g): "Having a marijuana concentration of 6 or more" in blood within 2 hours of cessation) — PROPOSED ONLY, not enacted. The HB 34 history rests on a secondary tracker and is labelled as such.
12.3 What law prohibits (KRS 189A.010(1), current): (a) alcohol ≥0.08 (≥0.02 if under 21) by scientifically reliable breath/blood test within 2 hours of cessation; (b) under influence of alcohol; (c) under influence of any other substance/combination impairing driving ability; (d) presence of controlled substance listed in subsection (12) detected in blood by scientifically reliable test within 2 hours of cessation; (e) combined influence of alcohol + impairing substance Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/25RS/sb230/orig_bill.pdf As written. The jacketed bill text quotes the current (1)(a)–(e) before proposing (g); the (1)(c) impairment prong is the marijuana prong (see next row).
12.3 Marijuana-specific nuance [VERIFY pinpoint]: secondary analyses state KRS 189A.010(12) list EXCLUDES marijuana from presence-only prong, so marijuana DUI must be proved by actual impairment (driving, behaviour/observations, field sobriety, blood evidence, expert testimony) rather than mere THC presence; blood THC number alone does not automatically prove impairment; official (12) list not re-opened verbatim — (12) list [VERIFY] on legislature site before reliance in a case; contrary "zero-tolerance" secondary reading not adopted; conflict preserved, not resolved by assertion Corrected https://dpa.ky.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/20240805-DUI-Manual-2024-EXTENDED-Update-FINAL-with-cover-and-letter.pdf Resolved in favour of the impairment reading: KRS 189A.010(12)(a) is "Any Schedule I controlled substance except marijuana," followed by the named substances (alprazolam, amphetamine, buprenorphine, butalbital, carisoprodol, cocaine, diazepam, hydrocodone, meprobamate, methadone, methamphetamine, oxycodone, promethazine, propoxyphene, zolpidem). The Kentucky Department of Public Advocacy DUI Manual states expressly: "Because 1(d) specifies that marijuana will never fall into this subsection, it will always be prosecuted under 1(c)." The "zero-tolerance for marijuana" reading is therefore rejected, not merely preserved. Note for the federal baseline: marijuana is expressly excepted in (12)(a) whether non-medical marijuana is Schedule I or state-licensed medical marijuana is Schedule III — the (12) text does not depend on the federal schedule. See G12-03 (resolved).
12.3 Medical card is no driving defence: KRS 218B.035 preserves DUI prosecution; OMC General Questions: cardholders may not operate vehicles/machinery while under influence, keep cannabis in arm's reach when operating machinery, or use if it impairs safe task performance; prescription-drug-like rights for state/local-law drug testing (KRS 218B.045(1)) do not extend to driving while impaired Confirmed https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/General-Questions.aspx ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf As written. KRS 218B.035(1)(a)–(d) (operating/consuming while operating, arm's-reach possession, negligent/malpractice tasks) and §218B.035(4) (nothing supersedes DUI laws, including KRS 189A.010) support the statement.
12.3 First-offence DUI penalties (secondary summary via Drugged Driving Resources PDF, 2018 — [VERIFY] current penalty text): first within 5 years $200–$500 and/or 48 hours–30 days county jail; second $350–$500 + 7 days–6 months; third $500–$1,000 + 30 days–12 months; fourth+ Class D felony, mandatory minimum 240 days; general DUI penalties, not THC-specific, summary dated — re-check before quoting Unverified https://dpa.ky.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/20240805-DUI-Manual-2024-EXTENDED-Update-FINAL-with-cover-and-letter.pdf Keep as Unverified (G12-04): the figures match secondary summaries, but the enrolled KRS 189A.010 penalty text was not opened in this audit. Do not quote the penalty ladder as confirmed law.
12.4 No Kentucky medical-cannabis expungement programme and no automatic (non-petition) marijuana expungement statute located; no provision in Chapter 218B creating expungement for pre-legalisation offences; what exists is the general framework, enterable only on ordinary conditions Confirmed https://www.kycourts.gov/AOC/Information-and-Technology/Pages/Expungement.aspx?sfnsn=mo As written (negative finding, retained). No automatic marijuana expungement statute was located in this audit either.
12.4 First-possession sealing — KRS 218A.276(8)–(11): person convicted of possession of marijuana (also synthetic drugs/salvia), court may set aside/void conviction on satisfactory completion of treatment/probation/other sentence + certificate; voided conviction not deemed first offence or conviction for disqualifications/disabilities; court shall order sealing of all records in court custody and any other agency/official including law enforcement (except KRS 27A.099), on AOC form; agencies certify sealing within 60 days of order; after sealing proceedings shall not be used against defendant, agencies reply no record exists, person need not disclose on employment/credit/other applications; inspection thereafter only by court permission or subject's motion, only to persons named in motion Confirmed https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-431/section-431-073/ Substance confirmed as stated; source note: the original cites FindLaw reproduction of §218A.276 and this audit did not open the enrolled legislature page for §218A.276, so the pinpoint should be re-opened at republication, but the substance is corroborated by the National Reentry Resource Center Kentucky summary (first marijuana possession voided/sealed under KRS 218A.276(1),(8),(9)). The rewrite retains the substance without a flag, and this row records the pinpoint caveat.
12.4 General misdemeanour expungement — KRS 431.078: person convicted of misdemeanour/violation/traffic infraction (or series from single incident, or series not from single incident) may petition convicting court for expungement within that judicial district, including dismissed/amended charges in the action; except KRS 218A.275(8)/218A.276(8), petition no sooner than 5 years after sentence completion or successful probation completion, whichever later; hearing no sooner than 30 days after filing, notice to county attorney, identified victim, others with relevant information; single-incident court shall order expungement if (among §4 conditions) offence not sex offence or offence against child, no previous felony conviction, no other misdemeanour/violation conviction in 5 years before conviction sought (full §4/§5 conditions not fully extracted — [VERIFY] full text before advising eligibility) Confirmed https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-431/section-431-073/ As written, with the §4/§5 full-conditions flag retained in the rewrite as a narrow eligibility-check note (the 5-year, hearing, notice and single-incident conditions above are as stated; do not advise on multi-incident petitions without the full §5 text).
12.4 Felony expungement — KRS 431.073 (general, secondary summary): single specified Class D felony (or series from single incident) may be expunged 5 years after sentence completion; record for offence receiving full pardon may be expunged; whether given marijuana trafficking/cultivation felony (e.g. ≥5 plants, Class D) is "specified" eligible felony under §431.073 list not confirmed [VERIFY against eligible-offence list] — do not promise felony marijuana expungement Corrected https://www.kycourts.gov/AOC/Information-and-Technology/Pages/Expungement.aspx?sfnsn=mo ; https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-431/section-431-073/ Partly resolved: KRS 431.073(1)(a) expressly lists KRS 218A.1423 (marijuana cultivation) and KRS 218A.500 (paraphernalia) among eligible Class D felonies, and (1)(d) provides a catch-all for a Class D felony (or pre-1 Jan 1975 offence punishable by ≤5 years) that is not a KRS 189A.010, 508.032 or 519.055 violation, abuse of public office, sex offence, offence against a child, and did not result in serious bodily injury or death. A ≥5-plant cultivation felony under §218A.1423 is therefore expressly listed; a trafficking felony under §218A.1421 is NOT in the (1)(a) list, so its eligibility depends on the (1)(d) catch-all and case-specific facts — keep that narrow flag only. The 5-year filing rule (after sentence completion or successful probation/parole, whichever later) is confirmed. See G12-05 (partly resolved).
12.4 Dismissed charges: criminal offence dismissed without prejudice may be expunged after 3 years (felony) / 1 year (misdemeanour) per National Reentry Resource Center Kentucky summary (secondary) — official pinpoint [VERIFY] Unverified https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-431/section-431-073/ Keep as Unverified (G12-05, dismissed-charge limb): secondary summary only; the enrolled KRS 431.076 text was not opened.
12.4 Certification: every expungement petition/application shall include certification of eligibility from Department of Kentucky State Police + Administrative Office of the Courts, certifying background check conducted and whether petitioner eligible (KRS 431.079(1)) Confirmed https://www.kycourts.gov/AOC/Information-and-Technology/Pages/Expungement.aspx?sfnsn=mo As written (kycourts.gov describes the certification process; the §431.079(1) pinpoint is carried from the original).
12.4 Proposed, not law: SB 33 (2025) would have removed penalties for possession/cultivation/trafficking up to 8 oz / 5 plants and created new Chapter 431 marijuana-expungement process (retroactive in part) — 2025 bill, not law, must not be presented as current relief; HB 420 / SB 186 (earlier adult-use bills with expungement sections) likewise dead/proposed only (Run 1 Part 1 pattern) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/25RS/sb230/orig_bill.pdf As written in substance (SB 33 cited in original via legislature record page; this audit did not re-open SB 33's record, but no enactment was found and the bill is presented only as proposed in the rewrite). Do not present SB 33, HB 420 or SB 186 as law.
12.4 Governor's pardons (Run 1): conditional-pardon executive order for out-of-state medical purchases (EO 2022-798) rescinded effective 1 July 2026 by EO 2026-361 (Run 1); no general marijuana-conviction pardon programme replacing it located [UNAVAILABLE] Corrected https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/laws-and-regulations/Pages/Executive-Orders.aspx ; https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/General-Questions.aspx Confirmed and dated from the official OMC page: EO 2026-361 issued 11 June 2026 rescinds EO 2022-798 (issued 15 Nov 2022); beginning 1 July 2026, Kentuckians with certain conditions who purchase medical cannabis out-of-state are no longer eligible for the conditional pardon for marijuana possession under KRS 218A.1422, and cardholders purchasing from an out-of-state dispensary may be subject to law enforcement action. The "no replacement programme located" negative is retained. The [UNAVAILABLE] on the rescission itself is removed.
12.5 Who may consume: only registered qualified patients, visiting qualified patients and designated caregivers acting for the patient, within supply limits (Run 1); diversion to non-cardholder prohibited; cardholder who sells/distributes/dispenses to person not permitted to possess/use shall have card revoked + criminal prosecution (915 KAR 2:010, citing KRS 218B.075(1)) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/002/020/ As written (Run 1 finding, carried; supply quantities confirmed in §12.6 row below).
12.5 Smoking banned everywhere for patients: using/consuming by smoking unauthorised; violator shall not be considered in possession/use of medicinal cannabis, shall not benefit from Chapter 218B protections, may face card revocation + prosecution under KRS 218A.1421/1422 (KRS 218B.035(1)(g) via Run 1); odour of uncombusted raw plant material is not evidence of smoking (Run 1) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf As written. HB 829 text confirms §218B.035(1)(g) (smoking) and the odour provision (odour/smell of uncombusted raw plant material shall not constitute evidence of smoking).
12.5 Vaporising: 21+ only, not in public places / public transport (Run 1); exact current pinpoint for public-place / public-transport vaping ban not re-extracted verbatim — carried as Run 1 finding, pinpoint [VERIFY] (candidate sources KRS 218B.035, 915 KAR 1:070); do not drop rule, do not upgrade pinpoint without check Corrected https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf Pinpoint resolved: KRS 218B.035(1)(h) prohibits using/consuming marijuana by vaping while on any form of public transportation, in any public place as defined in KRS 525.010, or in any place of public accommodation, resort, or amusement as defined in KRS 344.130. The 21+ purchase rule is separate (915 KAR 1:070, §12.2). The [VERIFY] on the vaping-ban pinpoint is removed. See G12-01 (resolved).
12.5 OMC published prohibited-place list (General Questions, opened in original): cardholders may not operate vehicles/machinery while under influence; keep cannabis in arm's reach when operating machinery; use if it impairs safe task performance; possess/use on school property unless school policies allow registered patients to use at school administered by school nurse/appropriate staff; possess/use at correctional facilities or on federal property; consume by combustion (smoking); grow own without cannabis business licence Confirmed https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/General-Questions.aspx ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf As written. The school limb is now governed by KRS 218B.045(4)(c) district policy (§12.10), and the arm's-reach / machinery limbs match KRS 218B.035(1)(a)–(d).

12.5 Hemp-derived consumption: no HDCP/CIB on-premise consumption rule located (see §11.7(B)); CIB by-the-drink sales ended 1 Jan 2026 (Run 1) — package-only consumption off-premises is CIB model found Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/902/045/190/14787/ As written (Run 1 finding for the 1 Jan 2026 date, carried; the no-rule negative is retained). Note the food-service provision in 45:190 (registered pre-packaged adult-use ingestibles offered as ready-to-consume at food service establishments; adult-use cannabinoids shall not be added to ingestible food at the establishment) is a retail/food-service rule, not a consumption-lounge licence.
12.5 Private-property rule (bridge to §12.7): KRS 218B.040(1)(e) expressly does not prohibit person/employer/corporation/other entity occupying/owning/controlling property from prohibiting/regulating use, consumption, possession, transfer, display, transportation, sale, growing of medicinal cannabis on/in that property (except as provided in KRS 218B.045) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf As written in substance (the §218B.040(1)(e) property-control principle is stated in the original and is consistent with the §12.7 analysis; the enrolled pinpoint should be re-opened at republication alongside §12.7, but no contradiction was found).
12.6 Visiting qualified patient definition/proof (Run 1, KRS 218B.010 / 218B.025 / 218B.055): person registered as such through Cabinet OR possessing valid out-of-state registry card + documentation of qualifying-condition diagnosis; dispensary may dispense to visiting patient presenting card + documentation even without Kentucky card (1:070, Run 1) Confirmed https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-218b/section-218b-055/ ; https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/FAQs/Pages/Patient-and-Caregiver-Questions.aspx As written, strengthened: KRS 218B.055(5) provides a person with a valid out-of-state card + diagnosis documentation may use the out-of-state card for all purposes in the chapter and shall NOT be required to apply for or receive a Kentucky visiting-patient card. Presentation at the dispensary is therefore a statutory route, not merely a Run 1 reading.
12.6 Limits (Run 1, 915 KAR 2:020): visiting patients ≤10-day supply per 8 days (vs in-state ≤30-day per 25 days); in-state 10-day = 37.5 g raw / 9.5 g concentrate / 1,300 mg THC — visiting 10-day is same 10-day quantity measure, difference is purchase frequency (8 days vs 25 days for 30-day supply); outside residence product in original dispensary container + carry valid registry card (visiting: out-of-state card + diagnosis documentation) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/002/020/ ; https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/FAQs/Pages/Patient-and-Caregiver-Questions.aspx As written, now primary-confirmed: 915 KAR 2:020 defines daily supply 3.75 g raw / 1 g concentrate / 130 mg THC, 10-day supply 37.5 g / 9.5 g / 1,300 mg, 30-day supply 112 g / 28 g / 3,900 mg; OMC Patient/Caregiver FAQ states a visiting qualified patient may only purchase a 10-day supply during a given 8-day period. Non-consumable topicals (ointments, soaps, lotions, other topical agents) do not count toward supply limits.
12.6 Visiting-patient age [VERIFY]: secondary guide states Kentucky accepts out-of-state cards from visitors 21+; primary provisions opened in Run 1 / this pass do not state 21+ visiting floor in excerpts extracted; do not publish 21+ as visiting rule without primary pinpoint — 21+ rules that ARE primary are vaporising purchase (21+) and HDCP/CIB purchase (21+) Corrected https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-218b/section-218b-055/ ; https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/FAQs/Pages/Patient-and-Caregiver-Questions.aspx ; https://kymedcan.ky.gov/patients-and-caregivers/Documents/2024-03-14 Qualified Patient & Designated Caregiver Guide v.1.pdf Resolved: a person is eligible to apply for a registry card as a visiting qualified patient if not a Kentucky resident or resident <30 days, AT LEAST 21 YEARS OF AGE, not convicted of a disqualifying felony, possessing a valid out-of-state card + qualifying-condition diagnosis documentation (KRS 218B.055(4); OMC Patient/Caregiver FAQ lists the same five criteria). The 21+ visiting floor is therefore a primary rule, not secondary-only. The apparent tension with KRS 218B.110 dispensary verification (verify presenter is at least 18 and is the cardholder) is a verification step, not a visiting-eligibility floor. See G12-02 (resolved).
12.6 No reciprocity list / no visiting-patient registration portal detail located [UNAVAILABLE]: whether visiting patient must pre-register vs present at dispensary, and whether any state's card excluded, not confirmed beyond card + documentation rule; out-of-state patients may not bring home-state cannabis into Kentucky as matter of course (Part 10); report does not authorise importation Corrected https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-218b/section-218b-055/ Narrowed: pre-registration is NOT required for a holder of a valid out-of-state card + diagnosis documentation (KRS 218B.055(5) — may use out-of-state card for all purposes, no Kentucky visiting card required). A Kentucky visiting card is an optional application route (OMC FAQ: application, documentation, $25 fee, 1-year card). Whether any particular state's card is excluded remains unlocated — keep only that limb (G12-02, narrowed). Importation is not authorised (see also §12.4 pardon rescission).
12.6 Cardholder protections on road (KRS 218B.030): possession/application for registry card (or out-of-state card, or business licence) shall not constitute probable cause/reasonable suspicion nor support search of person/property/home (without prejudice to probable cause on other grounds); rebuttable presumption of lawful use where cardholder holds valid card (or visiting card + diagnosis documentation) and possesses no more than allowed amount Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf As written (Run 1 finding, carried; consistent with the HB 829 framework).
12.7 No Kentucky landlord/tenant statute protecting medical-cannabis use in rented housing located; governing provision points other way: KRS 218B.040(1)(e) preserves property occupier/owner/controller right to prohibit/regulate use, consumption, possession, transfer, display, transportation, sale, growing on/in property (except KRS 218B.045); landlord may by lease/property rules ban smoking, vaping, possession or growing; tenant has no Chapter 218B right to override ban on text found Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf As written.
12.7 What KRS 218B.045 does protect (and does not): §218B.045(1) prescription-drug-like rights ONLY for drug testing required by state/local law; (2) custody/visitation/parenting (no denial, no presumption of abuse/neglect/dependency for permitted conduct, absent clear-and-convincing evidence of unreasonable danger to child); (3) authorised use equivalent to other practitioner-directed medication for medical care including organ transplants, health facilities may develop policies permitting on-premises use; (4) school enrolment (see §12.10); NONE mentions housing, tenancy, eviction or rent — housing-protection claim under Chapter 218B [UNAVAILABLE] on sources opened Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf As written. The §218B.045(1)–(4) structure is confirmed in the enrolled HB 829 Acts text (2024 Ky. Acts ch. 195, §4).
12.7 General tenancy overlay (not cannabis-specific, flagged not surveyed): KRS Chapter 383 (including URLTA as adopted in certain jurisdictions) + federal housing rules (e.g. federally assisted housing, where federal Schedule I/III status matters) not surveyed; may independently restrict/permit action against tenant, particularly smoking; federal assisted-housing consequences [VERIFY] before advising tenant in public/federally assisted housing — do not advise state card protects federal tenancy Unverified https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf Keep as Unverified (G12-10). Baseline note for the rewrite: state-licensed medical marijuana is Schedule III under the given baseline, but that does not by itself answer a federal assisted-housing question, and no HUD/Kentucky housing guidance was opened — do not advise that a state card protects a federal tenancy.
12.7 Growing in rented property: home grow prohibited for all (Run 1), so tenant has no lawful home-grow right to assert against landlord; landlord ban on growing consistent with state law, not in tension with it Confirmed https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/General-Questions.aspx As written. OMC General Questions: "Can I grow my own medical cannabis? No. Kentucky law prohibits individuals from growing their own medical cannabis."
12.7 Hemp in rented property: no hemp-specific landlord/tenant rule located [UNAVAILABLE]; general property-control principle in KRS 218B.040(1)(e) is medical-cannabis provision, does not by its terms govern hemp/CBD possession in rental Unverified https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf Keep as Unverified (G12-12, landlord limb).
12.8 Kentucky state law: no state firearms disqualification for cardholders found; no Chapter 218B provision disqualifies registered/visiting patient from owning/possessing firearms under Kentucky law; medical programme and firearms licensing systems not linked in sources opened (secondary dispensary guidance: Kentucky law does not prohibit cardholders from possessing/owning firearms; applying for medical card does not require forfeiting firearm/permit); no Kentucky statute creating state safe harbour for cardholder's federal firearms purchase located Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf As written (negative findings, retained). The secondary dispensary guidance is labelled secondary in the rewrite.
12.8 Federal law: conflict live; 18 U.S.C. §922(g)(3) unlawful for person "who is an unlawful user of or addicted to any controlled substance" to ship/transport/possess/receive firearms/ammunition in/affecting commerce; ATF Form 4473 asks unlawful-user question; ATF 2011 open letter: state marijuana authorisation card is reasonable cause to believe person is unlawful user (secondary summaries); late-2024 ATF officials warned Kentucky residents participating in then-imminent medical programme would be prohibited from buying/possessing firearms federally, existing owners not "expected to" turn firearms over but must "make decision to divest" to follow federal law (Marijuana Moment, 30 Jan 2026, reporting 2024 warning + bipartisan Kentucky resolution urging Congress to amend — no action taken as reported) Confirmed https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/laws-and-regulations/Pages/Executive-Orders.aspx Substance retained with source honesty: the §922(g)(3) text and Form 4473 question are federal law; the 2011 open letter, the 2024 Kentucky warning and the resolution account rest on secondary reporting as the original states. No safe harbour is claimed.
12.8 Schedule III effect — [VERIFY], do not assume: fixed baseline is state-licensed medical marijuana moved to Schedule III 28 Apr 2026; whether that move alone removes Kentucky medical patient from §922(g)(3) "unlawful user" category, or whether ATF issued Kentucky-specific/general safe harbour for Schedule III medical users, not resolved from primary ATF/Federal Register source; secondary sources still describe federal prohibition as applying to medical users (Veriheal; LegalClarity citing ATF 2026 interim rule that person who "ceased regularly unlawfully using" is not unlawful user, no bright-line abstinence period) Unverified https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf Keep as Unverified (G12-07, Schedule III limb), restated under the given baseline: ATF's interim final rule effective 22 Jan 2026 rewrote 27 CFR 478.11 to require regular use continuing into the present; a person who has ceased regularly unlawfully using, or whose use is isolated/sporadic, is not an "unlawful user" under that rule, with no bright-line abstinence period stated. That rule does NOT by itself create a safe harbour for a currently-using Kentucky medical patient, and no ATF Kentucky-specific or Schedule III medical-user safe harbour was located. A currently, regularly using patient therefore still faces the state-lawful / federally-prohibited conflict on purchase and possession.
12.8 Practical position: Kentucky patient faces state-lawful / federally-prohibited conflict on purchase and possession; card expiry + cessation of use is only route described in secondary sources for falling outside §922(g)(3), with no defined waiting period; litigation (e.g. United States v. Baxter, cited in secondary sources as pending) may change this, but no Supreme Court holding resolving it for Kentucky patients was located in this pass [VERIFY on ATF / court sources before advising any patient to purchase or retain firearm] Corrected https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf Corrected: the "no Supreme Court holding" sentence is deleted. Under the given federal baseline, United States v. Hemani, No. 24-1234, was decided 18 June 2026 (Gorsuch): a status-only §922(g)(3) prosecution of a regular marijuana user for in-home possession, with no danger showing, is inconsistent with the Second Amendment (as-applied, narrow). Hemani does NOT hold that all Kentucky medical patients may purchase or possess firearms, does NOT address purchase from a dealer, possession outside the home, or the Schedule III question, and does NOT create a safe harbour. Baxter's outcome remains unlocated — keep that narrow flag only. Do not advise any patient to purchase or retain a firearm on the basis of Hemani.
12.8 Caregivers: designated caregiver who does not personally use cannabis is not "unlawful user" on statute's terms (secondary analysis), but may still face point-of-sale denial if dealer treats card possession as reasonable cause — practical obstacle, not legal disqualification on sources opened [VERIFY] Unverified https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/24RS/HB829/SCS1.pdf Keep as Unverified (secondary analysis only).
12.8 Enhanced penalties note (not gun-ownership rule): KRS 218A.992 enhances certain drug offences where offender possessed firearm at time (court example: possession + paraphernalia, each Class A misdemeanours, enhanced to Class D felonies by firearm-possession finding) — patient whose conduct falls OUTSIDE Chapter 218B protection (smoking, over-limit possession, diversion) therefore faces compounded exposure compliant patient does not; official pinpoint [VERIFY] Unverified https://law.justia.com/cases/kentucky/supreme-court/2012/2010-sc-000713-mr.html Keep as Unverified for the §218A.992 pinpoint (court-example basis only, as the original states). The Class A misdemeanour premise is now confirmed (Blane, §12.1 row).
12.9 No Kentucky veterinary cannabis / pet-CBD statute or regulation located: no law (a) authorising veterinarians to prescribe/recommend cannabis for animals, (b) creating pet-CBD category with own THC limit/labelling/registration, or (c) banning pet CBD; medical cannabis under Chapter 218B is for human registered/visiting patients only; giving patient's medicinal cannabis to animal would be diversion outside Chapter 218B protection Confirmed https://kbve.ky.gov/about-kbve/Pages/statements-announcements.aspx As written (negative findings, retained).
12.9 KBVE position (official board page): Board cautions selling/prescribing/advising on CBD in animals is at your own risk if patient has adverse reaction; background: 2018 Farm Bill descheduled hemp, crop regulation to USDA-approved state plans; CBD/hemp extracts/derivatives regulation remains with FDA under FD&C Act; until FDA clear written statement or federal law defines extract products as supplement vs drug, "Kentucky will continue to view CBD as a supplement and treat it accordingly" (citing KRS 218A.010(23)–(24), KRS 260.850, KRS 260.852); no prohibition in Kentucky for carrying product in store/clinic as off-label-use product; hemp-grain/extract regulation in animal feed remains with AAFCO + UK DRS Feed Program; UK DRS Feed Program policy statement 26 Sept 2023 "Current Policy on Use of Hemp Products in Animal Feed" — contact UK DRS directly (policy text not opened [VERIFY]) Confirmed https://kbve.ky.gov/about-kbve/Pages/statements-announcements.aspx As written, except the UK DRS policy TEXT remains unopened — keep that narrow limb (G12-09, feed-policy limb). The KBVE statements themselves are confirmed on the official board page.
12.9 Product legality baseline for pet products: "In Kentucky, CBD products are legal when derived from industrial hemp (Cannabis sativa L. with THC ≤0.3% dry weight)" (KBVE, same page); that is hemp definition, not pet-product approval; pet product >0.3% delta-9 THC dry weight is not hemp; intoxicating HDCP sold for animal use would still be adult-use (21+) human product under 45:190 on framework found — no animal-use HDCP rule located [UNAVAILABLE]; human CBD products should not be assumed safe for dogs/cats (secondary veterinary-safety guidance, Bluegrass Hemp Oil / Kentucky Cannabis Company, Oct 2025): discuss with licensed veterinarian, bring label + batch COA + ingredients + medication history; THC exposure can be dangerous for dogs/cats, may require urgent care; safety recommendations, not Kentucky law, marked as such Confirmed https://kbve.ky.gov/about-kbve/Pages/statements-announcements.aspx As written. The veterinary-safety guidance is labelled secondary in the rewrite.
12.9 Federal hemp-date note for pet products: pet CBD product hemp under pre-11 Dec 2026 definition but >0.4 mg total THC per container would fall outside post-11 Dec 2026 federal hemp definition (Run 1 baseline) — no Kentucky pet-specific response to that date located [VERIFY] Corrected https://kbve.ky.gov/about-kbve/Pages/statements-announcements.aspx Wording corrected for the baseline split (12 Nov 2026 effect, limited until 11 Dec 2026 to non-naturally-produced/synthesized exclusions; full total-THC definition + 0.4 mg/container cap after 11 Dec 2026). The Kentucky-response flag is retained.
12.10 Enrolment protection (KRS 218B.045(4)(a)–(b), effective 1 Jan 2025): school shall not refuse to enrol or otherwise penalise person solely for cardholder status, unless failing to do so would violate federal law/regulations and cause school to lose monetary/licensing-related benefit under federal law/regulations; school shall not be penalised or denied any benefit under state law for enrolling cardholder Corrected https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf Corrected by addition from the enrolled HB 829 text: §218B.045(4)(a) also excuses a school where enrolment would violate "the school's sincerely held religious beliefs, if the school is a private, religious institution." The original omits that second excuse. Both excuses are now stated.
12.10 On-property use — district policy, statute wording changed [VERIFY exact amended text]: SB 47 original summary required each local board / public charter board, no later than 1 July 2024, to "establish policies to permit" pupil who is registered patient to consume on school property as deemed necessary by parent/legal guardian, administered by school nurse or under appropriate staff supervision; later KSBA model policy 09.2242 (2024) reflecting HB 829 (2024) creating KRS 218B.045 frames choice as EITHER prohibit OR permit (effective 1 Jan 2025); if permits, policy shall: (1) require administration (a) by school nurse or under appropriate staff supervision, OR (b) by parent/legal guardian, and (c) out of view of other students; (2) include process by which nurse/staff may by written acknowledgement (09.2242 AP.2) refuse to administer/supervise; KSBA issue paper 13 Aug 2024 describes HB 829 as requiring board policy by 1 Dec 2024 to either permit or prohibit Corrected https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf ; https://portal.ksba.org/public/Meeting/Attachments/DisplayAttachment.aspx?AttachmentID=846183 Resolved: the operative rule is NOT "all schools must permit." Under KRS 218B.045(4)(c) as amended by HB 829 (2024 Ky. Acts ch. 195, effective 1 Jan 2025): each local board of education, each board of directors of a public charter school, AND the governing body of each certified nonpublic school shall, no later than 1 December 2024, establish policies related to use of medicinal cannabis by a pupil who is a registered qualified patient on school property. Policies shall EITHER prohibit use on school property OR permit use by a registered-patient pupil as deemed necessary by the parent/legal guardian. A permitting policy shall: (1) require administration (a)(i) by a school nurse or under supervision of appropriate school staff, or (ii) by the parent/legal guardian, and (b) out of view of other students; and (2) include a process by which a school nurse or other staff member may refuse to administer or supervise administration. The July 2024 "permit" deadline was the SB 47 original; the December 2024 "permit or prohibit" deadline is the HB 829 amendment — different enactments, not a contradiction. Nuance: "written acknowledgement" is KSBA form AP.2 language, not statute text (statute says "a process by which … may refuse"). The [VERIFY] on the statutory subsection is removed; the district-by-district list remains open. See G12-06 (resolved, narrowed).
12.10 Possession/use default (OMC): cardholders may not possess/use on school property UNLESS school policies allow registered patients to use at school, administered by school nurse/appropriate staff (OMC General Questions); school buses, preschool/primary/secondary grounds, correctional facilities, federal property appear in pre-SB 47 bill summaries as prohibited places; SB 47 / HB 829 school-policy regime above is current framework — do not cite 2019 bill summary as current law Confirmed https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/General-Questions.aspx ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf As written. Note KRS 218B.035(1)(e)(1) states the school-grounds prohibition "except as permitted in accordance with policies enacted pursuant to KRS 218B.045(4)" — consistent with the district-policy rule.
12.10 Under-18 patients generally: registered patient under 18 shall not possess/purchase/acquire medicinal cannabis, shall only use with assistance of designated caregiver who is parent/legal guardian responsible for consent for medical treatment (KRS 218B.025(2)); persons under 18 may not enter/remain on cannabis-business premises (KRS 218B.095(2)(c)) Confirmed https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/030/ As written.
12.10 Hemp-derived products in schools: no school-specific HDCP rule (e.g. CBD in schools) located [UNAVAILABLE]; general school tobacco/drug policies of district + 21+ adult-use HDCP rule (§12.2) are only adjacent rules found — adult-use HDCP may not lawfully be sold to school pupil in any event Unverified https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/902/045/190/14787/ Keep as Unverified.

Part 2 — Corrected rewrite: Kentucky Cannabis & Hemp, Parts 0–12

Federal baseline, Governing Facts, Part 0 and Part 1

Conventions: [VERIFY] = uncertain/conflicting/not confirmed on the official page itself. [UNAVAILABLE] = no such source or figure was located. Same-name-place rule applied throughout: all places are Kentucky places (Lexington KY not VA; Louisville KY not CO; Frankfort KY not IL; Bowling Green KY not OH; Richmond KY not VA; Florence KY not SC/AL; London KY, Georgetown KY not DC/TX, Glasgow KY not Scotland, Paris KY not France).

Federal baseline (fixed context, not re-researched — used as given)

Split scheduling: state-licensed medical marijuana and FDA-approved products moved to Schedule III effective 28 April 2026 (91 FR 22714). All adult-use marijuana remains Schedule I. The broader 2024 rescheduling proposal is not final. IRS §280E is generally lifted for Schedule III medical activity; adult-use remains fully subject to §280E. Hemp: PL 119-37 §781 takes effect 12 November 2026, but PL 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026. After 11 December 2026, the full total-THC hemp definition and the 0.4 mg total THC per container cap apply. USDA enforcement of DEA-registered lab testing for hemp is delayed to 31 December 2026. The federal medical marijuana appropriations rider runs through 11 December 2026. There is no federal cannabis banking law.

How Kentucky's Schedule III / §280E change applies (analysis, not a Kentucky statute): Because Kentucky's programme is state-licensed, its cultivators, processors, producers, dispensaries and safety compliance facilities conducting medical activity fall on the Schedule III side after 28 April 2026, so §280E — which by its terms reaches only Schedule I/II trafficking — no longer disallows their ordinary deductions federally. Any activity outside the medical programme (non-patient possession, any adult-use sale, and, after 11 December 2026, most intoxicating hemp-derived products that cease to be "hemp" federally) remains Schedule I federally and remains fully within §280E. Kentucky has no adult-use licensee to whom the Schedule I side could attach, and no Kentucky §280E-decoupling statute was located [UNAVAILABLE — absence not proved]. Whether Kentucky's IRC conformity picks up the federal change for state tax, and for which tax year, is [VERIFY] with the Department of Revenue — do not advise on it from this report.

Stale OMC FAQ — do not quote as current. The Office of Medical Cannabis (OMC) Banking and Taxes FAQ still quotes the pre-April-2026 §280E text (Schedule I/II trafficking) and has not been updated for Schedule III: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/Banking-and-Taxes-Questions.aspx — treat its tax paragraph as stale. Kentucky has not, in sources found here, published a state-level conformity/implementation statement for the April 2026 Schedule III order.

Kentucky and the 12 November / 11 December 2026 hemp dates: No Kentucky statute or executive order found in this audit purports to override or cushion the federal dates. As of 28 October 2026 Kentucky operators have no enacted state cushion for 11 December 2026 located in primary sources; the next regular session (2027) falls after the federal effective date. See §1.6.5 for the full mechanics.

0.8 Hemp beverages moved to ABC; 5 mg cap; package-only. SB 202, 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 82 (not ch. 98), signed 25 March 2025: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/25rs/sb202.html ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/25RS/documents/0082.pdf — created "cannabis-infused beverages" (CIBs): no more than 5 mg of intoxicating adult-use cannabinoids per 12-ounce serving, for adults 21+, sold by the package only, in wet territory. A CIB retail package licence "shall only be issued as a supplemental license to the holder of a quota retail package license" and authorises sale by the package for off-premises consumption only: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=55923 — Distribution and retail sale are regulated by the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control under KRS 243.401 (created 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 82, sec. 6, effective 25 March 2025). CIBs bear a $1.92-per-gallon excise under KRS 243.720 effective 1 July 2025, plus an 11% wholesale sales tax under KRS 243.884: https://revenue.ky.gov/Business/Alcohol-Taxes/Pages/default.aspx — Current CIB licence fees (HB 775, ch. 98, sec. 32): retail package $2,000/yr, distributor $1,000/yr, distributor supplemental $1,000/yr, direct shipper Type B $1,000/yr; the SB 202 as-enacted fees ($500/$520/$100) are history only. Fair/festival by-the-drink window ended 1 Jan 2026 (Acts ch. 82, §38 — see §1.6.4). Note: ch. 98 is a separate 2025 act (HB 775) that amended KRS 243.720 (sec. 20, effective 1 July 2025); it is not SB 202's chapter.

0.10 Federal hemp cliff as Kentucky's near-term exposure (industry estimates, not primary-confirmed). The following are industry/testimony figures reported secondarily and are not confirmed on a primary source: a 15 Oct 2026 Interim Joint Committee appearance, a Kentucky hemp market of >$300m, >3,000 jobs, and ~95% of consumer demand in THC products, and the industry's 2027 asks — each remains [VERIFY] against the committee minutes. What is governed by the federal baseline given for this audit is: PL 119-37 §781 takes effect 12 Nov 2026 but is limited by PL 119-103 §2019 until 11 Dec 2026, after which the full total-THC hemp definition and the 0.4 mg total THC per container cap apply. No Kentucky statute or executive order cushioning those dates was confirmed; that negative claim remains [VERIFY] against any post-15-Oct statement by the Governor, KDA or ABC. The $300m Kentucky estimate is a different scope from the $739m U.S. figure in §0.11 and is not a contradiction.

0.11 Hemp agriculture 2025. Kentucky planted 4,800 acres of industrial hemp in 2025: http://www.nass.usda.gov/Publications/Todays_Reports/reports/hempan26.pdf (USDA National Hemp Report, 16 Apr 2026). The county count (60), the ~98% retail end-use share, 160 growers, 40 processors, 9,000 approved acres and the +60% year-on-year approved-acreage claim remain [VERIFY] against KDA releases/lists; approved acreage and planted acreage are different measures and must never be merged (4,800 planted vs an unverified 9,000 approved). U.S. hemp production value in 2025 was $739 million, up 64% from 2024, for production in the open and under protection: http://www.nass.usda.gov/Publications/Todays_Reports/reports/hempan26.pdf — That is a U.S. figure, not a Kentucky figure.

0.12 Licence-lottery inquiries. The Auditor of Public Accounts announced an inquiry on 17 Apr 2025 and the same day wrote to OMC that it was conducting a preliminary assessment of the licensing application process; OMC supplied records in May and Oct 2025: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/transparency/Pages/default.aspx — No Auditor final report was located on auditor.ky.gov; the Auditor's outcome remains Unavailable (route in §3). Separately, the Finance and Administration Cabinet's Office of Inspector General, at OMC's request, independently reviewed the process and reported on 7 May 2026 that it was thorough, fair and fully transparent, with no anomalies or irregularities, and recommended a formal debrief before any second round: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/transparency/Documents/5.7.26_2025-OIG-002%20CHFS%20OMC%20Investigation%20Report%20and%20Department%20Response.pdf — The OIG outcome is not the Auditor's outcome and must not be substituted for it. The out-of-state-dominance complaint is not attributed to the Auditor on any primary source located [VERIFY].

0.13 Medical cannabis is exempt from Kentucky sales and excise taxes at the till — OMC Banking and Taxes FAQ: "Medical cannabis will be exempt from sales and excise taxes": https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/Banking-and-Taxes-Questions.aspx — cited as an OMC statement; no KRS section for the exemption was located in this audit. Hemp/CIB tax treatment is not established on a listed primary page in this audit [VERIFY — see Part 2]. The CIB $1.92/gallon excise is confirmed via HB 775, ch. 98, and the Department of Revenue (see §0.8); the CIB general 6% sales-tax treatment [VERIFY].

0.14 Federal Schedule III / §280E consequence for Kentucky — see Federal baseline above. Kentucky has no adult-use licensee; the Schedule III/§280E benefit therefore attaches in Kentucky only to state-licensed medical activity. No Kentucky §280E-decoupling statute was located [UNAVAILABLE]; state IRC conformity [VERIFY] with the Department of Revenue. The OMC FAQ §280E text is pre-April-2026 wording and is stale: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/Banking-and-Taxes-Questions.aspx

PART 1 — LAWS (corrected)

1.1 Legal status: medical only

Medical cannabis is legal for registered qualified patients, visiting qualified patients and designated caregivers acting within KRS 218B, and for licensed cannabis businesses acting within KRS 218B and 915 KAR Chapter 1: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=54279 — Everything else is not legal for non-patients: possession by a non-cardholder is charged under KRS 218A.1422 [Class B misdemeanour, max 45 days — mirror text only, VERIFY on the legislature 218A.1422 page; fine ≤$250 under KRS 534.040 — mirror only, VERIFY]; trafficking (KRS 218A.1421) and cultivation (KRS 218A.1423) are separate, escalating offences [mirror only — VERIFY]; no decriminalisation provision was located in the retrieved primary text [UNAVAILABLE]; no adult-use market; no home grow (even for patients): https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/General-Questions.aspx — no recreational purchase age for medical cannabis (hemp-derived products have their own 21+ rule, see §1.6.3). Smoking raw plant material is prohibited even for patients: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf (§218B.035(1)(g)).

Hemp is a separate legal category: industrial hemp (≤0.3% delta-9 THC dry weight, KRS 260.850) [VERIFY on the legislature KRS 260.850 page] and hemp-derived cannabinoid products complying with 902 KAR 45:190 / HB 544 and, for beverages, SB 202, are lawful for adults 21+ (see §1.6.3) — but that lawfulness is state law only and is directly threatened federally after 11 Dec 2026 (Federal baseline above). A product lawful as hemp in Kentucky today can still be a Schedule I substance federally if it is not medical and not hemp under the post-11-Dec definition.

KRS 218A.1422 carve-out (text as reproduced in mirrors — legislature page to be opened before quoting as official): "(1) A person is guilty of possession of marijuana when he or she knowingly and unlawfully possesses marijuana, and the possession is not in compliance with, or otherwise authorized by, KRS Chapter 218B. … (3) This section does not apply to: (a) A cannabis business or a cannabis business agent, as defined in KRS 218B.010, when acting in compliance with KRS Chapter 218B; or (b) A cardholder, as defined in KRS 218B.010, whose use of medicinal cannabis is in compliance with KRS Chapter 218B." [VERIFY on the legislature KRS 218A.1422 page.]

1.3 Penalties, cultivation, consumption, product forms

Possession — non-patients (KRS 218A.1422) [mirror only — VERIFY on the legislature page]. As reproduced, any knowing unlawful possession not authorised by 218B is a Class B misdemeanour, maximum 45 days' incarceration (notwithstanding the usual 90-day Class B cap in KRS 532.090 — [VERIFY]), fine ≤$250 under KRS 534.040(2)(b) [mirror only — VERIFY]. There is NO amount tier inside §218A.1422 itself as reproduced: 1 gram and 7 ounces are the same offence class. The amount matters only at the trafficking threshold: possession of 8 ounces or more is prima facie evidence of intent to sell/transfer (KRS 218A.1421(5)) [mirror only — VERIFY] — a presumption supporting a trafficking charge, not a separate possession tier. Secondary summaries describing "up to 8 ounces = misdemeanour" are shorthand for this presumption.

Trafficking — KRS 218A.1421 [mirror only — VERIFY on the legislature page]: <8 oz: 1st = Class A misdemeanour (≤12 months, ≤$500), 2nd+ = Class D felony; 8 oz–<5 lb: 1st = Class D felony (1–5 years), 2nd+ = Class C felony (5–10 years); ≥5 lb: 1st = Class C felony, 2nd+ = Class B felony (10–20 years). Felony fines generally $1,000–$10,000 [general sentencing/fine provisions — VERIFY on KRS 532.060 / 534.030 pages]. Trafficking in or within 1,000 feet of a school building used primarily for classroom instruction is a Class D felony unless a more severe penalty applies (KRS 218A.1411) [mirror only — VERIFY; measurement straight-line from the nearest wall].

Cultivation — KRS 218A.1423 [mirror only — VERIFY on the legislature page]. As reproduced, knowingly planting/growing/harvesting with intent to sell/transfer: <5 plants: 1st = Class A misdemeanour, 2nd+ = Class D felony; ≥5 plants: 1st = Class D felony, 2nd+ = Class C felony; ≥5 plants is prima facie evidence of purpose of sale/transfer. Below 5 plants, intent must be proved by other evidence. Home grow is prohibited for everyone, including registered patients and caregivers: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/General-Questions.aspx ("Kentucky law prohibits individuals from growing their own medical cannabis"); "use of medicinal cannabis" by a cardholder does not include cultivation: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf (§218B.010(37)(b)). HB 401 (2026), which would have allowed home grow, died and is NOT law (see §1.10).

Public consumption / smoking / vaping. Smoking (combustion) of raw plant material is prohibited for ALL patients, everywhere: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf (§218B.035(1)(g)). OMC: "Kentucky law prohibits individuals to consume raw plant material by smoking and requires all raw plant materials packaged in the Commonwealth to be labeled as 'not intended for consumption by smoking'": https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/FAQs/Pages/Patient-and-Caregiver-Questions.aspx — 915 KAR 1:030 requires the same label ("NOT INTENDED FOR CONSUMPTION BY SMOKING"): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/030/14969/ — A person who violates §218B.035(1)(g) (smoking) or (1)(h) (public vaping) "shall not be considered to be in possession of medicinal cannabis or engaged in the use of medicinal cannabis and shall not benefit from the legal protections afforded by this chapter" (§218B.035(3)(a)). Odour of uncombusted raw plant material is NOT evidence of smoking (§218B.035(3)(b)).

Vaping: allowed as a product form, but only for cardholders 21+ — 915 KAR 1:070 §1(3)(c): a dispensary "shall not sell or dispense medicinal cannabis products intended for consumption by vaporizing to a cardholder who is younger than twenty-one (21) years of age or to a designated caregiver for [a patient] younger than twenty-one": https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/070/ — and vaping is prohibited on public transport, in any public place as defined in KRS 525.010, or in any place of public accommodation, resort, or amusement as defined in KRS 344.130 (§218B.035(1)(h)). Vaporising by a 21+ cardholder is permitted except in those prohibited places (a private home is an example, not the sole permitted place). Public-place consequence (§218B.035(3)(c)): if an individual smokes or vapes in those public places, (1) the cabinet may revoke the registry identification card, and (2) the individual may be subject to prosecution under KRS 218A.1421 and 218A.1422. That revocation/prosecution limb is tied to the public-place conduct, not to all smoking.

Other prohibited conduct (KRS 218B.035(1), 2024 Ky. Acts ch. 195): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf — (a) operating/navigating/being in actual physical control of a vehicle/aircraft/vessel (or other machinery-powered transport device) while under the influence; (b) consuming while operating/navigating/in actual physical control; (c) possessing within the operator's arm's reach or requiring <2-step access while operating/navigating/in actual physical control; (d) undertaking a task under the influence where that would constitute negligence or professional malpractice; (e) possessing/using on preschool/primary/secondary school grounds except as permitted by policies under §218B.045(4) (see §1.9 for the permitting-policy detail), in any correctional facility, or on federal property; (f) using marijuana if not a registered or visiting qualified patient; (g) smoking (above); (h) public vaping (above); (i) cultivating unless licensed as a cannabis cultivator/producer (or agent) under KRS 218B.080/085/090. Penalty for (1)(a)/(b) = the same as KRS 189A.010 DUI penalties (§218B.035(2)).

Dispensaries may not allow self-administration on premises (915 KAR 1:070): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/070/

Allowed medical product forms and THC limits (915 KAR 1:070 §1(3)(f) for dispensaries; same caps for processors in 915 KAR 1:040): Raw plant material Δ9-THC ≤35%; edible/oil/tincture for oral consumption ≤10 mg Δ9-THC per serving; any other medicinal cannabis product Δ9-THC ≤70%; any product must NOT contain vitamin E acetate. (KRS 218B.120 states the same caps for producers, but its text was located only in a Justia mirror in this audit — the caps above are confirmed via the KAR, not via §218B.120.) OMC product list: "Allowable medical cannabis products include edibles, oils, tinctures, vapes, and raw plant material. Only individuals over the age of 21 are able to purchase vaping products": https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/FAQs/Pages/Patient-and-Caregiver-Questions.aspx — Topicals/ointments/soaps/lotions do not count toward supply limits (915 KAR 2:020 §1(2)): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/002/020/ — No per-package THC cap for edibles beyond the 10 mg/serving rule was located — [VERIFY whether 915 KAR 1:100 imposes a package cap].

1.4 Medical programme

Qualifying conditions — original six (KRS 218B.010(26), 2024 Ky. Acts ch. 195, §1): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf — (1) Any type or form of cancer, regardless of stage; (2) Chronic, severe, intractable, or debilitating pain; (3) Epilepsy or any other intractable seizure disorder; (4) Multiple sclerosis, muscle spasms, or spasticity; (5) Chronic nausea or cyclical vomiting syndrome that has proven resistant to other conventional medical treatments; (6) Posttraumatic stress disorder; (7) Plus: "Any other medical condition or disease for which the Kentucky Center for Cannabis established in KRS 164.983, or its successor, determines that sufficient scientific data and evidence exists to demonstrate that an individual diagnosed with that condition or disease is likely to receive medical, therapeutic, or palliative benefits from the use of medicinal cannabis" (§218B.010(26)(g)) — the statutory Center-determination pathway.

2026 clarification (regulation, not merely an executive-order list): EO 2026-318 (2 June 2026) directed OMC to issue an emergency regulation clarifying §218B.010(26); OMC's FAQ notes the EO "clarifies the statutory definition of 'qualifying medical condition'": https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/FAQs/Pages/Patient-and-Caregiver-Questions.aspx — 915 KAR 2:050E §1 and ordinary 915 KAR 2:050 §1(2) (filed 9 September 2026) then list 15 conditions "recommended for express inclusion … by the Kentucky Board of Physicians and Advisors and … recognized as having at least one underlying symptom that is defined as a 'qualifying medical condition' under KRS 218B.010(26)": https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/downloads/docs/18083/document.engrossed.pdf ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/downloads/docs/18469/document.markup.pdf — Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis; Parkinson's Disease; Crohn's Disease; Ulcerative Colitis; Sickle Cell Anemia; Cachexia or Wasting Syndrome; Neuropathies; Severe Arthritis; Fibromyalgia; Muscular Dystrophy; Huntington's Disease; Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV); Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS); Glaucoma; Terminal Illness. The regulation does not amend §218B.010(26) itself, and its underlying-symptom theory is distinct from the Center-determination pathway in (26)(g). Reported legislative challenge to the Governor's authority to do this by executive order [secondary — Unverified; no court ruling or AG opinion located in this audit — cross-ref §0.6]. No anxiety, insomnia or autism addition was located as enacted law [UNAVAILABLE].

Practitioner authorisation / written certification (KRS 218B.050; OMC practitioner guidance). Practitioner = a physician or an advanced practice registered nurse authorised to prescribe controlled substances under KRS 314.042, who applies to the same state licensing board (Board of Medical Licensure / Board of Nursing) for authorisation to provide written certifications: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=54617 (§218B.050(1)) — board authorisation and programme registration are both required. The practitioner must: establish a bona fide practitioner-patient relationship (§218B.050(4)(a)); diagnose or confirm a diagnosis of a qualifying condition for which the patient is likely to receive safe and effective therapeutic or palliative benefit (§218B.050(4)(b)); review the electronic-monitoring (KASPER, KRS 218A.202) report covering at least the preceding 12 months (§218B.050(4)(c)); consult on risks/side effects including interactions with other drugs/medications (§218B.050(4)(d)); and obtain custodial parent/guardian consent for a minor (§218B.050(4)(e)). A bona fide relationship may be established after a primary-care referral and maintained via telehealth, but shall not be established via telehealth (§218B.050(5)). Initial written certification must be provided during an in-person examination; subsequent certifications, including for renewal, may be provided electronically or via telehealth (§218B.050(6)(b)) — no same-practitioner limitation appears in that text. A written certification for applying for a card is valid for not more than 60 days; the practitioner may renew it for not more than three additional periods of not more than 60 days each; thereafter a new certification requires an in-person or telehealth examination (§218B.050(6)(c)); issuance must be recorded in the electronic monitoring system within 24 hours (§218B.050(6)(d)). There is no categorical contraindication bar in final KRS 218B.050. §218B.050(7) bars only dispensing and certifying a family member or oneself; §218B.050(8)(c) makes failure to properly evaluate history/condition "including all prescription drugs that the patient is currently taking" sanctionable. A practitioner may recommend MORE than the standard 30-day supply if they reasonably believe the standard supply would be insufficient for uninterrupted therapeutic or palliative relief, documenting dosage and rationale: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/002/020/ ; excess at residence per regulations under KRS 218B.140(1)(c)6.: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=54279 (§218B.025(1)(b), (4)(b)). Practitioner fees are not an OMC fee [Unverified — OMC Renewals Guide to be opened]; secondary clinic price quotes are NOT official.

Cards, fees, validity (915 KAR 2:010; KRS 218B.055/060/065; OMC Patient and Caregiver Questions).

Card type Fee Validity / notes
In-state registered qualified patient $25 per application: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/002/010/ 1 year, unless the practitioner states an earlier date in the certification (KRS 218B.060(3); 915 KAR 2:010). Renewal application must be submitted no later than 30 calendar days before expiration (915 KAR 2:010) — not a "30–60 day window." Cabinet acknowledges receipt within 15 calendar days, approves/denies a complete application within 30 calendar days, and issues the card within 5 calendar days of approval (915 KAR 2:010; KRS 218B.065). Additionally requires: (i) diagnosis documentation from a practitioner other than the certifying practitioner, and (ii) custodial parent/guardian written agreement to allow use, serve as caregiver, and control acquisition/dosage/frequency: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf (§218B.055(7)). Patient must designate the caregiver in the patient's application; once that application is approved, the caregiver applies separately for each patient, with a signed notarised signature page pledging not to divert: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/002/010/ — Card 1 year unless the practitioner sets an earlier date for the connected patient: https://kymedcan.ky.gov:443/FAQs/Pages/Patient-and-Caregiver-Questions.aspx — Lost-card 10-day notify / 10-day replacement rule applies identically.

Two routes: (i) use a valid out-of-state registry identification card + qualifying-condition diagnosis documentation directly, with no Kentucky card required (§218B.055(5)); or (ii) obtain a Kentucky visiting card on the same $25/1-year terms. Eligibility for a KY visiting card: not a KY resident or KY resident <30 days; 21+; no disqualifying felony; valid out-of-state card + diagnosis documentation: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf (§218B.055(4)). Lost-card 10/10-day rule applies identically.

Disqualifying felony (KRS 218B.010(11), final Act): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/24RS/documents/0195.pdf — "(a) A felony offense that resulted in the person being classified by the Department of Corrections as a violent offender under KRS 439.3401; or (b) a violation of a state or federal controlled substance law classified as a felony where convicted, EXCEPT (1) an offense whose sentence (including probation, incarceration, or supervised release) was completed 5+ years earlier, or (2) an offense that, as determined by the cabinet, consisted of conduct this chapter would likely have prevented, where the conduct predated the chapter or was prosecuted by a non-Commonwealth authority."

Purchase / possession limits (KRS 218B.025 + 915 KAR 2:020).

Holder At residence On person Purchase window
Registered qualified patient 30-day supply 10-day supply Up to a 30-day supply in any 25-day period: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=54279 (§218B.025(6)(a))
Designated caregiver (per patient assisted) 30-day supply per patient 10-day supply per patient Up to a 30-day supply per patient in any 25-day period (§218B.025(6)(b)); may transport >10-day from dispensary to residence only in a sealed package requiring ≥2-step opening (§218B.025(4)(c))

Supply arithmetic (915 KAR 2:020 §1(1)): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/002/020/ — daily = 3.75 g raw / 1 g concentrate / 130 mg THC infused; 10-day = 37.5 g / 9.5 g / 1,300 mg; 30-day = 112 g / 28 g / 3,900 mg. Non-consumables (ointments, soaps, lotions, other topical agents) do NOT count (§1(2)). Note: 9.5 g ≠ 10×1 g; 112 g ≠ 30×3.75 g; 28 g ≠ 30×1 g — the regulation controls over arithmetic. A practitioner may recommend above the 30-day supply on the reasonable-belief standard above. Outside the residence, product must be in the original dispensary container and the cardholder must carry the valid registry card (visiting patients: out-of-state card + diagnosis documentation) (§218B.025(5)).

Out-of-state / visiting patients: A visiting qualified patient is a person with a valid out-of-state registry card (or equivalent) and documentation of a qualifying-condition diagnosis, who is allowed to use medicinal cannabis in their home jurisdiction (KRS 218B.055 framework; 915 KAR 1:070 dispensary rule: dispensary may dispense to a visiting patient presenting "a valid out-of-state registry identification card and documentation of having been diagnosed with a qualifying medical condition" even without a Kentucky card): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/070/ — Limits as above (10-day / 8-day). There is no general reciprocity that lets a Kentucky card be used to buy in another state — that is the other state's law. Kentucky residents buying out of state: see §1.5 (EO rescission).
