Renewal then costs the annual renewal fee each year. These totals are arithmetic on the official fees, not a separate official figure. Sources as in the table above.

4.2 Each medical licence type in detail

Cultivator — Tiers I–IV (KRS 218B.105; 915 KAR 1:030). What it allows: plant, grow, cultivate, harvest, trim, cure and store raw medicinal cannabis plant material in an enclosed, locked facility. A cultivator facility is not open to the general public. [VERIFY] in KRS 218B.105 and 915 KAR 1:030: the delivery-only-to-licensed-businesses rule, the safety-testing gate for deliveries, and any delta-9 THC cap on deliveries (the original report's 35% figure is not confirmed in this audit and is not repeated as fact here). Tier limits (statutory, KRS 218B.105): Tier I — indoor growth area not exceeding 2,500 square feet; Tier II — 10,000 sq ft; Tier III — 25,000 sq ft; Tier IV — 50,000 sq ft. Initial-round availability: Tier I 10, Tier II 4, Tier III 2, Tier IV 0. All 16 Tier I–III licences were awarded in the 28 October 2024 lottery (see §4.4). Current licensees (OMC page, 14 Oct 2026): Tier I 10, Tier II 4, Tier III 2 — the full initial allocation is still listed, though counties have changed through relocations/transfers. Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/licensees.aspx

Processor (KRS 218B.115). What it allows: acquire/purchase raw plant material from a cultivator, producer or another processor; possess, process, prepare, manufacture, manipulate, blend or package medicinal cannabis; transfer/transport/supply/sell medicinal cannabis and related supplies to other licensed cannabis businesses. A processor may not sell directly to patients/cardholders. Initial-round availability: 10. All 10 awarded 28 October 2024. Current licensees on the OMC page: 10. Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/licensees.aspx

Producer (KRS 218B.120). What it allows: the combined licence — cultivate (at the tier's indoor area) and process/package into usable product formats, at up to one cultivation facility and one processing facility per licence, which may be at separate locations (KRS 218B.080(4)(b)). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=54038 It is the only route to lawful vertical integration of growing + processing in Kentucky, and it exists in statute and regulation — but it was not offered in the initial application period. No producer licensee appears on the OMC licensee page (14 Oct 2026). Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/licensees.aspx When/if producers will be offered is [UNAVAILABLE] — no future window announcement was located. Fees: see the master table (application $5,000 + tier application fee; initial $25,000 + tier initial fee; renewal $25,000 + tier renewal fee; capital $150,000 + tier amount). Sources: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/ ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/010/15824/

Dispensary (KRS 218B.110). What it allows: purchase medicinal cannabis/products from licensed cultivators, processors, producers and other dispensaries as permitted, and sell/dispense to registered qualified patients and designated caregivers (and, per programme rules, visiting patients where applicable — that patient rule is Part 1 territory and is not restated here). Dispensaries are the only medical licence type subject to the 11-region system and the one-per-county rule (except Fayette/Jefferson). Initial-round availability: 48. Current licensees on the OMC page: 48. Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/licensees.aspx

Safety compliance facility (KRS 218B.125). What it allows: test medicinal cannabis for cannabinoid content and contaminants (every medical product must be tested before reaching cardholders, per programme description). It is the testing gate for cultivator deliveries. [VERIFY] the independence rule in KRS 218B.090 (principal officers/board members overlap with a cultivator, processor, producer or dispensary) before quoting it. Initial-round availability: no cap; no lottery for this category in the initial round because there was no cap. The first-ever Kentucky medical cannabis business licence was issued to a safety compliance facility — KCA Labs, September 2024. Source: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/KYGOV/bulletins/3c7aed1 Current licensees on the OMC page: 5 (KCA Laboratories LLC / KCA Labs, Fayette; Aquatic Laboratories LLC / Cannabusiness Laboratories, Fayette; STATE38 LLC, Graves; COMMONWEALTH ANALYTICS, Barren; Commonwealth Cannabis LLC, Marshall). Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/licensees.aspx

Any other medical licence type? No. KRS 218B.080(2) lists exactly the eight entries above (four cultivator tiers + dispensary + processor + producer + safety compliance facility). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=54038 There is no separate Kentucky medical "transporter", "distributor", "microbusiness", "delivery-only" or "research" business licence in Chapter 218B. Transport is an activity of a licensee, not a licence type. A "cannabis business agent" (employee/officer) registration exists in programme practice but is not a business licence type and is not counted here — [VERIFY] its current form in 915 KAR 1:010/1:020 if the dossier needs it.

4.3 Requirements common to all medical applicants/licensees

From 915 KAR 1:010 (application) and 915 KAR 1:020 (licence conditions). Sources: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/010/15824/ ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/

  • Age and criminal history. [VERIFY] in KRS 218B.010 and 915 KAR 1:010: the original report states no principal officer, board member, agent, volunteer or employee may be younger than 21 or have a disqualifying felony conviction (including violent-offender felonies under KRS 439.3401 and felony controlled-substance offences, with 5-year-completion and "conduct now lawful under Chapter 218B" exceptions), and that licensees must conduct criminal background checks before a person begins work. That detail was not re-read in a primary passage in this audit.
  • Site control. Evidence of a right to occupy the proposed location (deed, lease or contingency agreement) is required for a licence to be issued; the licence is site-specific. Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/Cannabis-Business-Questions.aspx
  • Business and ownership disclosure. Business plan; legal name/DBA, entity type, organisational structure and proof of registration with the Kentucky Secretary of State; an organisational chart showing all ownership interests including parent companies; disclosure of ownership/equity interests (a "10% or greater" threshold stated in secondary guides is [VERIFY] in 915 KAR 1:010, as it was not in the excerpt re-read); résumés/CVs for all principal officers and board members; express disclosure of any medicinal cannabis practitioner (physician/APRN) with an ownership, investment or compensation interest. Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/FAQs/Pages/Cannabis-Business-Questions.aspx
  • Sufficient capital. See master table. Proof is by funds on deposit or credit extension from one or more financial institutions; the same capital cannot support two applications. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/010/15824/
  • Insurance (before first day of activities). [VERIFY] in 915 KAR 1:020: the original report states workers' compensation for all Kentucky employees + Kentucky Office of Unemployment Insurance contributions; commercial general liability $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate; commercial automobile insurance as required by KRS 304.39-110 for any vehicle used to transport medicinal cannabis/products. That section was not re-read in this audit.
  • SOPs and records. [VERIFY] the full SOP list in 915 KAR 1:020 (original report lists security; recordkeeping; employee qualifications, supervision and training; quality assurance; adverse-event reporting and recall; waste disposal and sanitation; transportation; inventory management including storage and labelling; cash management and anti-fraud; odour mitigation and control; preventing unlawful diversion; and incident reporting). A licence must be conspicuously displayed at initial entry (915 KAR 1:020 general requirements). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/
  • Continuing capital. The licensee must continue to maintain sufficient capital for operations for at least the term of the licence.
  • Application mechanics (initial round). Online portal; Cabinet acknowledges receipt within 15 calendar days; deficiencies may be cured within 10 calendar days after notice (915 KAR 1:010 — cure period now confirmed, original [VERIFY] removed); Cabinet notifies approval/denial within 45 days of receiving a completed application. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/010/15824/ Denial grounds include failure to submit required materials, falsification, non-compliance with local §218B.130 prohibitions, and disqualifying principal officers/board members. Licence fees are payable within 15 calendar days of invoice; failure to pay means no licence issues. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/

4.4 Lottery process and results

How the lottery works (915 KAR 1:020 §3). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/

  • The Cabinet publishes notice on https://kymedcan.ky.gov of the number/category of licences available at the close of an application period and the application time frame.
  • Applicants who comply with KRS Chapter 218B and 915 KAR 1:010 and whose applications are deemed complete are eligible. If eligible applications do not exceed the licences available in a category, licences issue on timely fee payment — no lottery.
  • If eligible applications exceed available licences in a category, the Cabinet shall conduct a lottery for that category: eligible applicants are notified of lottery entry; the date, time and manner of random selection are publicly announced; the lottery is held in a manner observable by the public; the Cabinet may consult/contract with a third-party lottery operator or public agency with lottery expertise (in practice, the Kentucky Lottery Corporation); each eligible applicant is assigned a number kept confidential until after the drawings.
  • Selectees are notified in writing that a licence will issue on timely payment of the fee (within 15 calendar days of invoice; failure to pay = no licence). Non-selectees are notified in writing. If a selectee declines or fails to pay, the Cabinet may conduct supplemental lotteries from the remaining eligible applicants for that category until all licences are issued and paid.
  • Provisional licences for location-change cases: see §3.2 of the full report (120 days, non-transferable, no business activities authorised) — Part 3 territory, not restated here.

The initial application window and application volumes. Window: 1 July 2024 – 31 August 2024. Source: https://www.kentucky.gov/Pages/Activity-stream.aspx?n=GovernorBeshear&prId=2882 (OMC began accepting business applications 1 July 2024). Total applications: 4,998 in that window, confirmed by the Finance Cabinet OIG investigation report, which states it reviewed 4,998 applications and footnotes that 5,002 applications were submitted across both application periods, the second (safety-compliance-only) period accounting for 4. Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/transparency/Documents/5.7.26_2025-OIG-002%20CHFS%20OMC%20Investigation%20Report%20and%20Department%20Response.pdf By-category volumes are [VERIFY]: secondary reporting gives 584 cultivator, 344 processor and 4,076 dispensary applications, and separately 918 cultivator/processor applications (774 approved for the lottery) and 4,075 dispensary applications. Those splits do not reconcile cleanly to 4,998 (918 + 4,076 = 4,994; 918 + 4,075 = 4,993), and no primary by-category table was located. Do not publish a by-category total as official.

4.5 Are new applications open? Capped? Upcoming windows?

The initial application period is closed. It ran 1 July – 31 August 2024. All initial-round licences (16 cultivators, 10 processors, 48 dispensaries, plus uncapped safety compliance facilities) have been issued, subject to the transfers/relocations noted on the OMC licensee page. Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/licensees.aspx

No new application window, supplemental lottery, or Tier IV / producer offering had been announced in any official source located as of 25 October 2026. That is stated as a dated negative search result, not as a guarantee: OMC's stated mechanism is that the Cabinet "shall publish notice" on https://kymedcan.ky.gov of any future application availability, category and number of licences (915 KAR 1:020 §3). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/ Any claim of a 2026/2027 window is [UNAVAILABLE] until OMC publishes such a notice.

What is NOT capped: safety compliance facilities had no initial cap. Whether a safety compliance application can still be filed outside an "initial application period" is [VERIFY] — the regulation speaks of "initial license application availability" periods, and the OIG report records a second, safety-only application period (4 applications). Check OMC's current businesses page for a live safety-compliance application link.

Secondary-market route (not a new application): licences are transferable/saleable with OMC approval under KRS 218B.080(6) and 915 KAR 1:020 §10 — the OMC licensee page records many such transfers (e.g. Garry Kort → Ace 4 Target LLC, approved 14 Aug 2025, transferred 24 Sept 2025; Robert Hoogendyk → CB Slugger LLC; Thriveblue LLC → BD Expansion LLC; ZenLeaf Inc. → KYLX Acquisition Co. LLC). Sources: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/licensees.aspx ; https://kymedcan.ky.gov/businesses/Pages/Forms.aspx A would-be entrant can therefore acquire an existing licence by approved transfer even while new applications are closed. Transfer fees/conditions beyond OMC approval are [VERIFY] in 915 KAR 1:020 §10 (full text not read in this audit). Relocation within the same region (dispensaries) or to another county (non-region types) also requires prior OMC approval (915 KAR 1:020 §§3, 9). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/

4.6 ABC / CHFS licences and permits for hemp-derived cannabinoid products (non-beverage)

Regulatory split — read this first, because sources conflate it. Non-beverage hemp-derived cannabinoid products (delta-8, delta-9, THCA and other adult-use cannabinoid products sold at retail, plus ingestible/cosmetic products) are permitted/registered by the Cabinet for Health and Family Services, Department for Public Health, Food Safety Branch — not by ABC. ABC's hemp role is confined to cannabis-infused beverages (see §4.7). The CHFS hemp page states: "Manufacturers or Processors of Hemp-Derived Cannabinoids must follow the requirements set forth in 902 KAR 45:021E, including product registration" and "All adult-use cannabinoid products offered by retailers must be listed on the Cabinet for Health and Family Services Approved Product Registry." Source: https://chfs.ky.gov/agencies/dph/dphps/fsb/Pages/HDCP.aspx Whether the emergency version (45:021E) has been replaced by an ordinary regulation, and its current effective date, is [VERIFY] on the KAR page.

CHFS permits (902 KAR 45:021; 902 KAR 45:012 for retail). Sources: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/902/045/021/REG/ ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/902/045/012/15705/

Permit / registration Who needs it Fee (current regulation text) Key conditions
Hemp processing permit Person in Kentucky seeking to process hemp-derived cannabinoid products $3,000 (902 KAR 45:021 §1(b)4.a) Non-transferable as to person or address; posted conspicuously; renewed annually. Waived for facilities permitted as of 31 Dec 2024 until their next annual renewal.
Hemp manufacturing permit Person in Kentucky seeking to manufacture hemp-derived cannabinoid products $1,000 (§1(b)4.b) Same non-transferable / posted / annual-renewal conditions.
Hemp cannabinoid wholesale warehouse and distributor permit Wholesale/distribution of hemp-derived cannabinoid products $1,000 (§1(b)4.c) Same conditions.
Hemp cosmetic permit Hemp-derived cosmetic products $200 (§1(b)4.d) Same conditions.
Product registration Each adult-use cannabinoid product (or product class) offered at retail in Kentucky $200 per product or product class (902 KAR 45:021 §5) Registration via the CHFS Hemp Derived Cannabinoid Product Registry; a new registration and fee are required on changes to composition/formula, serving size/directions, or label. Products must be on the Approved Product Registry before retail sale. [VERIFY] the CHFS statement that a decision may take up to 90 days.
Out-of-state processor/manufacturer registration Out-of-state processors/manufacturers whose products are distributed in Kentucky The §1(b)4.c fee ($1,000) + product registration fee Must show a current valid home-state permit, the home-state regulation, and that home-state standards are equivalent to or exceed Kentucky's (per regulation text, home-state permit and regulation copies required); renewed annually by 31 December each year.
Retail establishment / food service establishment permit (adult-use cannabinoid products) Retailers and food-service establishments offering adult-use cannabinoid products $2,000 annual permit fee (902 KAR 45:012 §3(d)) Non-transferable as to person or address; renewed annually; every location must be permitted. Establishments registered before 31 December 2024 had the fee waived until next annual renewal. Retailers shall not be located within 1,000 feet of an elementary, middle or high school (pre-31 Dec 2024 registrants exempt). Retailers at a temporary event/festival without a cabinet permit must register ($250 temporary event registration fee) — 902 KAR 45:012. Products sold must be from an approved source, packaged/labelled per 902 KAR 45:021 §3, with a valid certificate of analysis available on request. [VERIFY] the employment-age rule in 902 KAR 45:012 (original report: no employee under 21 except a person 18+ under direct supervision of a person 21+).
Home-based processor Prohibited — "Hemp-derived cannabinoid products shall not be manufactured, marketed, sold, or distributed by a home-based processor" (902 KAR 45:021 §2(2) — citation corrected from 902 KAR 45:190, which is the packaging/labelling regulation). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/902/045/021/REG/

What a hemp retailer does NOT need: a medical cannabis (KRS 218B) licence, and — for non-beverage products — an ABC licence. A hemp retailer that also wants to sell cannabis-infused beverages needs the ABC retail package licence in addition (see §4.7), and only in wet territory through a quota retail package licence.

4.7 ABC licences for cannabis-infused beverages (CIBs) — SB 202 (2025)

Statute: 2025 SB 202, signed 25 March 2025, 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 82 (the "ch. 98" citation in part of the original report is removed). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=55923 (KRS 243.403 history: Created 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 82, sec. 7, effective March 25, 2025). The package-only retail regime operated from 1 June 2025 (sales only at quota retail package stores from that date; bars/restaurants lost authorisation then; by-the-drink sales at fairs/festivals/events in wet territory were allowed until 1 January 2026). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/25rs/SB202.html ABC was directed to promulgate its own CIB regulations by 1 July 2026; until then ABC administers the existing Department for Public Health regulations. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/804/004/400/REG/

Potency/channel rules that define the licences: CIBs contain no more than 5 mg of intoxicating adult-use cannabinoids per 12-ounce serving. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/25rs/SB202.html (HCS summary). Sales are package sales only, at licensed retail package stores with CIB authorisation, in wet territory; gas stations, convenience stores and smoke shops cannot sell CIBs; no by-the-drink sales at bars/restaurants (after the 1 Jan 2026 event exception expired). Purchasers must be 21+. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=55923 ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/25rs/SB202.html

Three-tier rule: manufacturer, distributor and retailer must operate exclusively within a single tier (with the direct-shipper exception below); a person/entity may not evade tier incompatibility through a second person/entity; the State Administrator examines ownership/membership/management and denies an application if the applicant is substantially interested in a holder of an incompatible licence (SB 202, KRS 243.040 as amended). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/25rs/SB202.html

ABC CIB licence types and fees (KRS 243.030, as amended by SB 202). The $500 retail / $520 distributor / $100 supplemental figures in the original report were House Committee Substitute 1 stage figures, not the enacted schedule, and are removed. The enacted schedule below is corroborated by 804 KAR 4:400's reference to the statutory amounts in KRS 243.030 and by 2026 General Assembly amendment summaries proposing to "reduce the annual license fee for a cannabis-infused beverage retail package license from $2,000 to $500" — confirming $2,000 as the current fee. Sources: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/804/004/400/REG/ ; https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/26rs/hb9.html [VERIFY] the enrolled SB 202 text / KRS 243.030 page itself for a verbatim quotation in the final dossier.

ABC licence What it allows Annual fee (KRS 243.030) Additional conditions

Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=55923 The 804 KAR 4:400 impact statement notes the number of quota retail package licences able to be issued is 1,888 — that is the ceiling on the number of businesses that could hold a CIB retail package licence, not a count of CIB licensees. KRS 217.039 reserves CIB manufacturer regulation/licensing to CHFS. 4.8 Social equity, local-ownership, and other preference provisions

There is no social-equity set-aside, preference, discount, or local-ownership requirement in Kentucky's medical cannabis licensing law. The initial allocation was by random lottery among complete, eligible applications, with no equity qualification, no scoring, and no equity provision in 915 KAR 1:020 §3. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/915/001/020/ No Kentucky statute or regulation located here gives a preference to Kentucky residents, to residents of the licence county, to small businesses, to veterans, or to persons with prior cannabis convictions. The only "preference-like" geographic rule is the dispensary-region allocation itself (at least 4 per region; 6 in Bluegrass/Kentuckiana with 2 in Fayette/Jefferson) and the one-per-county cap — those are access-spreading rules, not equity rules. Local-ownership: no city ordinance located here imposes a local-ownership requirement either. If a future local ordinance adds a residency/ownership test, it would need to be checked against the KRS 218B.130 "undue burden" limit — no such ordinance was found. Hemp/CIB: likewise, no social-equity or local-ownership preference was located in 902 KAR 45:021/45:012 or in the SB 202 CIB licensing framework.

Auditor/OIG review (completed, replacing the original [VERIFY]): the Auditor of Public Accounts announced a preliminary assessment of the lottery on 17 April 2025; OMC provided records on 30 May 2025 (over 580,000 pages) and 17 October 2025 (over 1.1 million pages); the Finance Cabinet Office of Inspector General issued an independent investigation report on 7 May 2026 (2025-OIG-002) reviewing OMC's licensing processes. Sources: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/transparency/Pages/default.aspx ; https://finance.ky.gov/office-of-the-inspector-general/Documents/5.7.26_2025-OIG-002%20CHFS%20OMC%20Investigation%20Report%20and%20Department%20Response.pdf The Auditor's own final report, if any, was not located — [VERIFY] Auditor of Public Accounts releases.

4.10 Adult-use licence types — PROPOSED ONLY (no adult-use licence exists in Kentucky law)

Kentucky has no adult-use licence type in force. The following are proposed only and must never be listed alongside the medical licences as if available. Under the federal baseline, any adult-use marijuana would remain Schedule I and fully subject to 280E even if Kentucky enacted such a law; no Kentucky adult-use licence exists to which Schedule III could apply.

Bill (2026 session) What it would have done Status
HB 198 (2026) Would have removed criminal penalties for possession of a personal-use quantity of cannabis and limited home grow, without setting up regulated sales. A retroactive-expungement provision was included. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/26rs/hb198.html DEAD — did not pass in the 2026 session; no enactment.
HB 199 (2026) Proposed constitutional amendment that would have enshrined the HB 198 rights in the state constitution and allowed the state to regulate sales. As a constitutional amendment it would have needed a three-fifths majority in each chamber plus voter approval; it would not by itself have created licences — the General Assembly would still have had to create the commercial framework. DEAD — did not pass; therefore no cannabis measure appeared on a 2026 statewide ballot via this route.
SB 168 (2026) Companion/parallel proposed constitutional amendment to HB 199 (same legislative-referral path). It would guarantee the right of a person 21+ to possess, use, buy or sell 1 ounce or less of cannabis and to cultivate, harvest and store up to 5 cannabis plants for personal use, while granting the General Assembly control over production, processing and sale. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/26rs/sb168.html DEAD — did not pass. Last action 5 Feb 2026: to Committee on Committees (S). Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/26rs/sb168.html
SB 223 (2026) Not an adult-use licensing bill — it would have regulated THC drinks more like alcohol: allow CIB retail package and distributor licensees (and DPH-approved manufacturers) to sell and serve CIBs at bars, restaurants, fairs and festivals, create a nonquota CIB supplemental drink licence, and cap sampling at 12 ounces per person per day. Source: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/26rs/sb223.html Did not become law. Included here only because it is sometimes misdescribed as "legalisation".

Consequence: there is no adult-use cultivator, processor, dispensary, or "dual-use" conversion licence to list, and no existing medical licensee may sell to non-patients. Any table in the dossier that lists "adult-use" licences for Kentucky must contain only PROPOSED rows, marked DEAD/PROPOSED.

5.0 Summary: what exists, what does not

Kentucky does not publish a single downloadable master register covering medical cannabis, hemp, hemp-derived cannabinoid products and ABC cannabis-infused beverages (CIB). Instead there are at least nine separate official systems, summarised first, then inventoried one by one in §5.1–§5.11.

Critical limitation, repeated for the whole of Part 5: the OMC licensee page, the dispensary directory, the practitioner directory and the CHFS REDCap registries are all interactive HTML/search pages with no export or download button identified in this pass. Anyone needing a machine-readable dataset must scrape the HTML (subject to the site's terms) or request the underlying data from the agency; do not present these pages as downloadable datasets.

PART 6 — MARKET DATA

6.0 Headline market picture (read this first)

Kentucky's medical market is ten months into retail sales (first-sale date secondary-reported only — see §6.1) and its hemp market is far larger and older but has contracted sharply from its 2019 peak on official processor-reported sales, even as 2024–2025 secondary estimates claim a recovery to roughly $300–330 million. The two stories must not be blended: medical sales are a new, small, tax-exempt retail market (Part 2 territory for tax treatment); hemp sales are processor-reported gross product sales dominated (in 2025, per secondary reporting) by hemp-derived retail products. Where an official figure exists it is used; where only a secondary figure exists it is labelled secondary with its date.

6.1 Medical sales since launch; active licences and dispensaries

Launch chronology: programme effective 1 January 2025 (SB 47, signed 31 March 2023) — Part 1 territory for full programme dates. Patient card applications accepted from 1 January 2025; practitioner directory launched 1 December 2024 (per the Governor's 16 December 2024 bulletin, authorised practitioners could begin issuing certifications on 1 December and the directory began 1 December). Source: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/KYGOV/bulletins/3c7aed1 First legal medical sale: 13 December 2025, The Post Dispensary, Beaver Dam (Ohio County) — secondary-reported only (MPP blog, 15 January 2026, and contemporary press). No OMC or Governor primary source for that date was located in this audit, so it is not presented as officially confirmed. The OMC Find a Dispensary page lists Tree Soft LLC (DBA: The Post Dispensary) as "open since January 16, 2026". Source: https://kymedcan.ky.gov/patients-and-caregivers/Pages/Find-A-Dispensary.aspx The directory does not state that 16 January 2026 is a reopening date, and no such inference is made here; both dates are carried with their sources and must not be overwritten by each other.

Medical sales totals:

  • No official OMC or Department of Revenue sales total or time series was located. Secondary analysis (CannBus Q3 2026) explicitly states OMC has not published a sales dashboard or report.   • Secondary monthly figures (Kentucky Cannabis Industry Alliance via press, 27 Aug 2026): approximately $1.87 million in July 2026, "tracking toward $2 million in August" 2026. These are industry-association figures reported in press, not official statistics — label them as such wherever used.

None of these is an official Kentucky figure.
  • Licence-fee revenue (official-context figure, secondary-reported): $27.5 million in application fees from 4,998 licence applications (July–August 2024 window), said by the Cabinet to cover staffing and IT (CannBus, citing Cabinet statements — [VERIFY against a Cabinet source]). This is fee revenue, not sales revenue, and it cannot be derived from the published application fees alone without the verified by-category application mix (see §4.4).

6.3 Official price data

No official OMC or state price series (average price per gram, per product type, or price index) was located. Secondary analysis (CannBus Q3 2026) states: "no average price per gram has been published." Secondary / anecdotal price points (label as such; do not average them): an eighth (3.5 g) at $52 in Kentucky (High Times price index analysis via press, 20 Sept 2026 — secondary, modelled index; the article attributes ~$34 of the $52 to "policy" i.e. limited store count/canopy — that attribution is editorial, not official). $130 for a 1 g THC vape cartridge in Kentucky vs $24 for a similar cartridge in Metropolis, Illinois — one patient's example reported in press (CannBus, citing press). Single-patient anecdote, not a market average. "$40 or more for edibles; $100 or more for vape products" — typical-retail characterisation in the same secondary report (press-sourced). ~14 Kentucky-grown brands on sale in August 2026 (CannBus, citing industry media) — brand count, not a price.

Why prices are high (secondary explanation, not an official finding): limited cultivation canopy (about 115,000 sq ft statewide across licensed tiers — arithmetic: 10 × 2,500 + 4 × 10,000 + 2 × 25,000 = 115,000 sq ft, before any operating-status adjustment), few open stores, and the end of out-of-state buying protection on 1 July 2026 (rescission of Executive Order 2022-798 by Executive Order 2026-361, 11 June 2026 — executive-order dates are Part 1 territory and are [VERIFY] in this slice). Treat the causal claim as secondary. Tax at the till (for price interpretation): medical cannabis is exempt from state sales and excise tax (OMC FAQ, per CannBus), so register price = shelf price before any local charge. Local sales-related charges were not checked in the secondary report [VERIFY for Part 2/Part 3].

6.5 Hemp-derived product market figures (official first; secondary marked)

Official figures: KDA processor-reported gross product sales (§6.4) are the only official hemp-market dollar series located: $193M (2019), $130M (2020), $43.4M (2021), $43.5M (2022). No official 2023–2026 processor-sales total was located. CHFS hemp licensing/product registration revenue 2026: >$2 million in 2026 (Kentucky Hemp Association presentation, reported by press 16 Oct 2026 — association figure, not a CHFS publication [VERIFY]). The same report states 14 employees administer the programme. Do not present as CHFS revenue without that attribution. Hemp-derived product composition 2025 (secondary, press 19 Oct 2026 citing KDA data): ~98% of Kentucky hemp produced was used for retail hemp-derived products (gummies, oils, tinctures, seltzers); 60 counties had hemp production. A separate association presentation (press, Oct 2026) puts cannabinoid floral material at ~97% of hemp grown — consistent in direction, different in precision; both are secondary attributions of KDA data. National hemp industry value 2025: $739 million, +64% vs prior year (USDA report, April 2026, as reported by press 19 Oct 2026). National, not Kentucky.

Secondary figures (dated, labelled — do not use as official): ~$330 million annually by 2025, >3,000 jobs (industry page, accessed 2026-10-25, undated; repeated by press 9 Sept 2026 as "valued at more than $330 million in 2025, according to one industry group"). Concept undefined (farm-gate? wholesale? retail?) — [VERIFY] before any use in Part 2/Part 6 of the parent dossier. ~$300 million market and 3,000 jobs at risk from federal THC restrictions (Kentucky Hemp Association framing via press, Oct 2026) — advocacy estimate, same order as the $330M figure but not the same number; the difference is not a conflict to resolve, it is two different advocacy framings. 2025 industry-page figures (160 growers, 40 processors, 9,000 approved acres, 4,700 planted, 4,690 harvested, 97.5% floral) — secondary page, undated, no KDA citation; planted/harvested acres are corroborated in round terms by press/KDA, the rest is not. CIB (beverage) market size: no Kentucky CIB sales, volume or tax-revenue figure was located (official or secondary) in this pass [UNAVAILABLE]. CIB excise tax exists under SB 202 (see Part 2), but no collections figure was found.

Federal-date note for the hemp-derived market (baseline as given, not re-audited): Public Law 119-37 §781 takes legal effect 12 November 2026, but Public Law 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026 to only the provisions excluding cannabinoids that are not naturally produced or are synthesized; the full total-THC definition and 0.4 mg per container cap apply after 11 December 2026. Kentucky's hemp-derived product market figures above predate those dates and must not be read as post-11 December 2026 market data. No Kentucky guidance on those federal dates was confirmed in this slice.

6.6 Cannabis-friendly banks and credit unions

  • No federal cannabis banking law has been enacted (federal baseline as given). No Kentucky state banking programme for cannabis was located, and no Kentucky-chartered bank or credit union publicly advertising cannabis banking in Kentucky was verified in this pass [VERIFY — this is a negative finding from search, not proof none exists].
  • What was found (secondary, national fintech, not a Kentucky bank): Safe Harbor Financial (SHF Holdings, Inc., NASDAQ: SHFS), a Denver-based fintech (not a bank — deposits held by partner banks/credit unions, FDIC/NCUA-insured to $250,000 per depositor per ownership category per its FAQ), named Kentucky among "new markets coming online" (with Delaware, Minnesota, Alabama, Mississippi) in a 3 March 2026 GlobeNewswire release reporting 29% YoY growth in emerging-market average deposit balances and 100+ new customer depository accounts across emerging markets. The release does not give a Kentucky-specific account count, deposit balance, or partner-bank name. Do not present Safe Harbor as a Kentucky bank or credit union, and do not attribute any Kentucky deposit figure to it.
  • Practical note for operators (from the federal baseline + programme structure): because Kentucky medical licensees are state-licensed, the April 2026 Schedule III move is the relevant federal change for 280E and, indirectly, for banking risk assessment — but no bank has been verified as changing Kentucky policy on that basis in the sources reviewed. Under the baseline, Schedule III applies to state-licensed medical marijuana only; adult-use remains Schedule I. Any bank/credit-union list for the parent dossier requires direct confirmation with each institution (and FinCEN guidance compliance), not a web list.
  • Hemp banking: hemp businesses bank through ordinary agricultural/commercial channels; no Kentucky-specific hemp-banking restriction or programme was located. The Kentucky Hemp Association's October 2026 proposals (reported by press) seek to extend to hemp farmers/businesses the financial-services protections established for the medical marijuana industry — a proposal, not law [VERIFY status].

Part 7 and Part 8

Last audited 28 October 2026. This rewrite keeps every subsection of the original Parts 7–8, with corrections applied in place. No "earlier research said X" notes appear in the main text; resolved flags have been removed and only still-unresolved items carry [VERIFY] or [UNAVAILABLE]. Every fact carries a source link next to it. No personal phone number or email for an individual is reproduced.

7.0 Federal hemp cliff — read this before §§7.5–7.6 (NEW, federal baseline as given)

Public Law 119-37 §781 takes legal effect 12 November 2026, but Public Law 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026 to only the provisions excluding cannabinoids that are not naturally produced or are synthesized. The full total-THC definition and the 0.4 mg per container cap apply after 11 December 2026. USDA has delayed enforcement of the DEA-registered-laboratory hemp testing requirement until 31 December 2026. (Federal baseline as given in the commission; not re-audited here.)

What that means for Kentucky: Kentucky's hemp-derived market as described in §§7.5–7.6 is a state-law market. Kentucky law permits, subject to CHFS registration and permits, adult-use cannabinoids including delta-8-THC, delta-10-THC, THCA (≤0.3% total THC), THCV, THCVA, delta-6-THC, HHC(-), THCP and THCM (902 KAR 45:021), and permits cannabis-infused beverages at up to 5 mg of intoxicating adult-use cannabinoids per 12 oz serving (SB 202 record). Kentucky's hemp definition itself is delta-9 only — Cannabis sativa L. "with a delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration of not more than three-tenths of one percent (0.3%) on a dry weight basis" (KRS 260.850(5) — statute text; official legislature page to be substituted on republication, see §3) — which is how a heavier gummy can hold 10–25 mg of delta-9 while staying at or under 0.3% by dry weight. None of that state-law arithmetic cushions the federal cliff: after 11 December 2026 a product that exceeds 0.4 mg total THC per container, fails the new federal total-THC definition, or is synthesized / not naturally produced is outside the federal hemp definition, whatever its Kentucky CHFS registration, KDA licence, or ABC CIB licence says. No Kentucky statute or order cushioning that cliff was located in this audit; no Kentucky guidance on the 12 November / 11 December 2026 dates was located either [VERIFY with KDA/CHFS/ABC — see §3]. The DEA-lab delay to 31 December 2026 is a federal enforcement delay: it does not waive Kentucky's own pre-harvest sampling, under which KDA itself collects the sample (302 KAR 50:021, 302 KAR 50:056). Readers must therefore treat every state-lawful potency and product in §§7.5–7.6 as state-lawful only, and re-check federal status after 11 December 2026 before relying on it for interstate shipment, banking, or tax positions.

7.1 Does Kentucky run its own USDA-approved state plan, or use the USDA programme?

Kentucky runs its own USDA-approved State Plan. It does NOT use direct USDA licensing. (USDA approved-plan list, updated 17 February 2026, listing "Kentucky | KY Approved Plan (pdf)*" — unlike states shown as "USDA Hemp Producer License".)

The plan document is the 15 September 2021 submission letter to USDA, stating Kentucky's State Plan was submitted "in advance of the implementation date of January 1, 2022, consistent with the state plan option … specifically in 7 U.S.C. § 1639p(a)(1)", and that the plan "consists of the statutory and regulatory framework for Kentucky's hemp program, specifically KRS 260.850 to 260.8691" plus seven administrative regulations. (Kentucky State Plan PDF) The reports/records regulation in that list is now cited as 302 KAR 50:046, not 50:045: 302 KAR 50:046 is titled "Department's reports to USDA; records retention for three (3) years" (302 KAR 50:046). The other regulations in the plan are 302 KAR 50:021 (growers), 50:031 (processors/handlers), 50:056 (sampling/testing; post-testing actions; disposal), 50:060 (fees), 50:070 (prohibited products), and 50:080 (materials incorporated by reference).

KDA's own 2026 processor orientation repeats: "Kentucky began operating under an approved State Plan January 1, 2022. All KY hemp regulations in 302 KAR 50 are incorporated into KY's State Plan." (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Orientation)

Consequence: for Kentucky, USDA does not maintain the operative grower/processor licence register; KDA does. USDA's role is plan approval, monthly producer reports from KDA (see §7.4), and national statistics. A person who wants to grow or process hemp in Kentucky applies to KDA, not to USDA. There is no Kentucky USDA-producer licence to list.

7.2 KDA hemp licences — the complete set

Under KRS Chapter 260 and 302 KAR Chapter 50 there are two KDA licence types. There is no third KDA hemp licence type (no separate KDA retailer licence, no KDA seed licence as a standalone type, no KDA "CBD licence"). Possession and retail sale of publicly marketable hemp products does not require a KDA licence at all (see §7.2.3). Everything else — living plants, viable seed, leaf/floral material, extracts above 0.3% THC — requires one of the two licences below.

KDA licence What it authorises (302 KAR 50:021 / 50:031) Who must hold it Key boundary
Hemp Grower License (302 KAR 50:021) Grow, handle (including drying, grinding, separating foliage from stem, storing, packaging) and market his or her own hemp. Licence-number format "21_0001" through "21_9999" [VERIFY against a KDA licence specimen/packet]. Any person who wishes to grow hemp at any location in Kentucky. "A Hemp Grower License shall not authorize the grower to process hemp, handle other person's hemp, or market another person's hemp." A grower who wants to process must also hold a processor/handler licence.
Hemp Processor/Handler License (302 KAR 50:031) Process, handle, broker, or market hemp that does not fall within the definition of a "publicly marketable hemp product". Scopes on the application "Plan" tab (2026 orientation): Grain Processing (crushing, dehulling, cold-pressing, etc.); Fiber Processing (decortication, making finished products from bales of stalk/stem); Floral Material Processing (extraction, formulation, crude refinement, distillation, any other modification of cannabinoid levels); Handler (brokers, labs, seed cleaners; bulk drying, milling, or separation of biomass as a service to others; storage or marketing of concentrated extracts). (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Packet) Any person who wishes to engage in processing, handling, brokering, or marketing of non-publicly-marketable hemp at any location in Kentucky. "Any person who does not hold a grower license from the department shall not grow, cultivate, or handle living hemp plants or other cannabis." A processor/handler licence does not authorise growing.

7.2.1 Grower licence — requirements, windows, renewal

Application: "Any person who wishes to grow hemp at any location in the Commonwealth shall submit to the department a completed Hemp Grower License Application, or annual license renewal, incorporated by reference as part of the Hemp Grower Licensing Application Packet in 302 KAR 50:080." Applications are delivered to KDA Hemp Licensing Program, 111 Corporate Drive, Frankfort, Kentucky 40601, or submitted online via the KDA hemp portal at www.kyagr.com/hemp. (302 KAR 50:021)

Application window / deadline: The regulation itself does not fix a calendar date; it says completed applications "shall be received by the department by the end of the application period established in the application" and the department "shall deny any Hemp Grower License Application that fails to meet the deadline established in the application." In practice the KDA application period ends 15 March for growers, and the renewal deadline in the regulation is also 15 March (below). The 15 March application deadline is therefore carried as the KDA packet date, not as a date in the regulation text — [VERIFY against the 2027 grower application packet when it is published]; do not cite 15 March as a 302 KAR 50:021 application-window date.

Renewal: "Existing grower license holders shall annually complete the department's requirements for license renewal by March 15." And: "A Hemp Grower License shall remain in force as long as the license holder meets annual renewal requirements by March 15 of each year." A licence "may be terminated by the license holder or the department upon thirty (30) days prior written notice." (302 KAR 50:021) This is a different date from the processor/handler renewal (31 December) — do not conflate them.

Age: "A person under the age of eighteen (18) years of age shall not apply for or hold a grower license." (302 KAR 50:021)

Residency / presence: The applicant's growing, handling and storage sites must be in Kentucky; the applicant's primary residence must be in Kentucky or within fifty (50) miles of at least one Kentucky growing site; the applicant must affirm residence at that primary residence from May 1 to September 30. (302 KAR 50:021)

Background check (statute + regulation) [VERIFY against the official KRS 260.862 page — the official page was not opened in this audit; the passage below rests on secondary mirrors and is not confirmed]: KRS 260.862(2)(d) is reported as: "An applicant for a license issued by the department shall submit to and pay for an annual criminal background check conducted by the Department of Kentucky State Police or another state or federal law enforcement agency or another entity selected by the department." KRS 260.862(2)(e) is reported as: "No person who has been convicted of any felony or any drug-related misdemeanor or violation in the previous ten (10) years from the date of application shall be eligible to obtain a license," with two 2014-pilot-programme exceptions (a person who was growing hemp lawfully under a Section 7606 pilot licence/registration/authorisation remains eligible; a person lawfully growing under Section 7606 before 20 December 2018 and convicted before that date remains eligible). KSP background-check cost is $20 per check [VERIFY against a KSP fee schedule — it was not opened in this audit]. The regulation adds: the background-check report must be delivered with the application or renewal; the department "shall not accept a report from a criminal background check that occurred more than sixty (60) days prior to the date of the application"; failure to submit it is grounds for denial; substitution of a signing authority requires department approval and a current background check on the substitute. (302 KAR 50:021)

Other evaluation criteria (302 KAR 50:021): complete application with all components; prior participants must have filed Field Planting Reports, Greenhouse/Indoor Planting Reports and Harvest Reports; willingness to comply with KDA and law-enforcement instructions; not delinquent in required reports or payments; no unpaid fees, fines or civil penalties owed to the department; no false statements (material falsification = ineligibility); proposed sites must comply with land-use restrictions (denial of all proposed sites = grounds for denial); and "The applicant shall not have had a hemp license revoked within five (5) years previous to the date of this application."

Mandatory orientation: "Applicants shall complete a mandatory orientation session at a location designated by the department. The department shall not allow any person to complete orientation in lieu of the applicant." A person is not a programme participant until the department has issued the licence following orientation and payment of licensing fees. (302 KAR 50:021)

What must be filed with the application: individual: full name, residential address, telephone, email (if available); business entity: entity name, EIN, Kentucky business location address and principal business location, signing-authority individual's full name/title/address/telephone/email, and each key participant's full name/title/address/telephone/email; proposed acreage or greenhouse/indoor square footage; street address, Location ID and GPS coordinates for each field, greenhouse, building or site where hemp will be grown, handled or stored; maps depicting each site with field boundaries and Location IDs corresponding to the GPS coordinates; agreement to all terms and conditions. (302 KAR 50:021)

"Storage only" growers — still [VERIFY]: Run 1 noted 130 of the 445 licensed growers in 2021 were "storage only" (licensed only to market a prior year's harvest). No regulation text located creates a distinct "storage-only licence" type; the more likely reading is that it was a KDA reporting category for growers who planted nothing that year but held a licence to store/market prior harvest. It is not counted here as a third licence type. [VERIFY against a KDA annual release that uses the term.]

7.2.2 Processor/handler licence — requirements, windows, renewal

Application: "Any person who wishes to engage in the processing, handling, brokering, or marketing of hemp that does not fall within the definition of a 'publicly marketable hemp product' at any location in the Commonwealth shall submit to the department a complete Processor/Handler License Application, or annual license renewal, incorporated by reference as part of the Processor/Handler License Application in 302 KAR 50:080." Paper applications go to KDA Hemp Licensing Program, 111 Corporate Drive, Frankfort, KY 40601; online applications via www.kyagr.com/hemp. (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Packet)

Application window: Unlike growers, processor/handler applications are accepted year-round. The KDA 2026 application packet states: "Hemp Processor/Handler License Applications accepted yearround." (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Packet)

Renewal: "Existing processor or handler license holders shall complete the department's requirements for license renewal by December 31." The 2026 packet's applicant acknowledgements repeat: "the annual renewal deadline for Hemp Processor/Handler Licenses is December 31 of each year." Annual renewal requires a new annual background check (2026 orientation: "Renewal of Processor/Handler Licenses require annual background check(s). The Licensing Fees are paid annually. The annual renewal is required by December 31 of each year. A license holder may terminate their license upon 30 days notice to KDA."). (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Packet, KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Orientation)

Age: "A person under the age of eighteen (18) years of age shall not apply for or hold a processor or handler license." (302 KAR 50:031, via KDA packet.)

Background check / eligibility [VERIFY on the official 302 KAR 50:031 page]: Same ten-year felony / drug-related-misdemeanour bar and annual KSP check as growers (see §7.2.1, itself flagged for the official KRS 260.862 page); the processor/handler evaluation criteria add: planned activities must remain compliant with state law and 302 KAR Chapter 50; adequate facilities or plans to acquire them; no hemp licence revoked within five (5) years previous to the application; no delinquent reports/payments; no unpaid fees/fines/civil penalties; no false statements; proposed sites must comply with land-use restrictions (denial of all proposed sites = grounds for denial).

Paper-application attachments (2026 packet): $200 service-charge check/money order payable to Kentucky State Treasurer (paper only); copy of driver's licence; KSP background check for applicant and all key participants, within the last 60 days; processing/handling/storage location maps (name, site address, Location IDs); Signing Authority form for business entities. (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Packet)

No live plants: A processor/handler licence does not authorise possessing living hemp plants — only a grower licence does. The packet's acknowledgements include: "a person shall not possess living hemp or other cannabis plants without a hemp grower license" and a licensed processor/handler "shall not allow another person, other than an agent of the licensed processor or handler, to process, handle or store hemp under their license in lieu of obtaining a separate hemp processor/handler license." (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Packet)

On expiry/termination: "if selected for participation in the program and my license is terminated or expires, then I will not be allowed to possess hemp in any form. I will be required to divest possession of all such hemp materials to an approved program license holder, or destroy all in-program hemp materials by the expiration or termination of my license." (KDA 2026 Processor/Handler Packet)

7.2.3 What needs NO KDA licence

"Possession and Retail Sale of Publicly Marketable Hemp Products does NOT require a license from KDA." (2026 orientation.) "Publicly marketable hemp product" (302 KAR 50:021) means a hemp product that: does not include any living hemp plants, viable seeds, leaf materials, floral materials, or delta-9-THC content above 0.3%; and does include, without limitation, bare stalks, bast fiber, hurd fiber, nonviable roots, nonviable seeds, seed oils, and plant extracts (excluding products containing delta-9-THC above 0.3%); or is CBD derived from "hemp"; or is CBD approved as a prescription medication by FDA. Conversely: "Hemp leaf material, floral material, and extracts above 0.3% THC are NOT Publicly Marketable Hemp Products and do require a hemp license to possess. Refer to 302 KAR 50:070 Prohibited Products." (302 KAR 50:021, KDA 2026 Orientation)

Important boundary for Part 7 readers: this KDA exemption does not exempt a retailer from the CHFS regime in §7.5. A shop selling delta-8 gummies needs no KDA licence (the gummies are a finished product, not leaf/floral material), but it does need a CHFS retail permit and the products must be CHFS-registered. The two systems answer different questions.

7.3 KDA fees — full schedule (302 KAR 50:060)

Regulation history line as shown on the official page: "(44 Ky.R. 1770; 2007; eff. 4-6-2018; 46 Ky.R. 2520; 47 Ky.R. 313; eff. 9-17-2020.)" All fees are nonrefundable. (Note: the current 50:060 page cross-refers to definitions in 302 KAR 50:020 §1 and 50:030 §1; the fee amounts are unaffected by that cross-reference numbering.)

Fee Amount Notes
Grower License Application fee Waived "$200 service charge for those applications submitted on paper. There shall be no service charge for applications submitted online." The 2026 packet confirms: "Application Fee is $0 (free)"; "Paper Application has a Service Charge of $200 (online applications, no service charge)".
Annual Grower Licensing Fee $400 for each growing address "This fee includes the first three (3) samples collected for THC testing from that growing address."
Secondary pre-harvest sample fee (grower) $250 for each additional sample "Beginning with the fourth sample, the Licensed Grower shall be invoiced for a secondary pre-harvest sample fee of $250 for each additional sample collected for THC testing." Also applies where a harvest is not completed within 30 days of sample collection and a new Harvest Report / secondary sample is required (302 KAR 50:021).
Retest fee $250 for each sample
Site modification surcharge — grower $750 for each GPS coordinate location change "for each GPS coordinate location change for each growing site after the grower licensing agreement has been executed." No surcharge is assessed for changes to storage-only locations.
Processor/Handler License Application fee Waived Same $200 paper service charge / $0 online as growers.
Annual Processor/Handler Licensing Fee — grain component $500
Annual Processor/Handler Licensing Fee — fiber component $500
Annual Processor/Handler Licensing Fee — floral material component (such as CBD) $3,000
Annual Processor/Handler Licensing Fee — handler (such as a seed cleaner or laboratory) $500
Multi-component processor Sum of each component "A processor for more than one (1) component (grain, fiber, or floral material) shall pay the licensing fee for each component. (For example, a person who processes hemp for fiber, grain, and CBD shall pay a participation fee of $4,000.)" ($500 + $500 + $3,000 = $4,000.)
Site modification surcharge — processor/handler $750 for each GPS coordinate location change "for each processing or handling site after the Processor/Handler application or renewal has been submitted."

Correction to a secondary figure: one secondary guide lists the floral-material processor fee as "$300". That is wrong; the official regulation text above says $3,000, and the $3,000 figure is used here. Do not use the $300 figure.

7.4 KDA grower plot/lot registration and pre-harvest sampling (summary — full operational rules are Part 11 territory; the licence mechanics are stated here)

Lot definition: "Lot" means "a contiguous area in a field, greenhouse, or indoor growing structure containing the same variety or strain of hemp throughout." (302 KAR 50:021)

Registration of every site: Growers must apply for licensing of all growing, handling and storage locations, including GPS coordinates, and receive department approval before having hemp on those premises. Site changes require a Site Modification Request, the applicable fee, and prior written approval before implementing the change. (302 KAR 50:021)

Minimums and buffers (licence conditions): minimum 1,000 plants in each growing site unless prior written approval; minimum one-quarter (0.25) acre in each outdoor growing site unless prior written approval; no growing in an outdoor field within 1,000 feet of a school or a public recreational area (exception: a school-designated vocational-agriculture instructor/qualified person whose proposal the school board voted to approve); no growing/handling/storage on a site not licensed; no growing within 100 feet of a residential structure without prior written department permission; no handling/storage of leaf or floral material in or adjacent to a residential structure; hemp physically segregated from other crops unless prior written approval; signage at each greenhouse, indoor growing location, storage building, and lot of one (1) acre or less showing agency title, licence-holder name, licence number and department telephone number. (302 KAR 50:021)

Reports: Field Planting Reports, Greenhouse/Indoor Planting Reports and Harvest Reports (all incorporated by reference in 302 KAR 50:080), plus any other reports the grower has agreed to. (302 KAR 50:021)

Pre-harvest sampling: "The grower shall not harvest hemp plants from a lot without the department first collecting samples from that lot." At least fifteen (15) days prior to anticipated harvest, the grower must submit a completed Harvest Report identifying the intended harvest date (or destruction date for a failed crop). Receipt triggers sample collection by a properly trained department representative under 302 KAR 50:056; the grower or authorised representative must be present. The grower must harvest not more than thirty (30) days following sample collection; failure to do so requires a new Harvest Report and may require a secondary pre-harvest sample fee. Floral materials "shall not be moved outside the Commonwealth, nor moved beyond a processor, nor commingled, nor extracted, until the department releases the material in writing." (302 KAR 50:021; the 30-day rule is corroborated by the KDA 2026 orientation: "Harvest must be completed within 30 days following preharvest sample collection.")

Testing / non-compliance (302 KAR 50:056, headline only — detail in Part 11): A sample exceeding the Acceptable Hemp THC Level is non-compliant. Within seven (7) days of notice of a result above that level but less than 1.000%, the grower must consent to destruction of all cannabis from that lot or request remediation and a post-harvest re-test (retest fee per 302 KAR 50:060 = $250). Samples at 1.000% or greater are not eligible for post-harvest retest and must be destroyed; refusal to comply with a destruction order is grounds for suspension/revocation; samples at 3.000% or greater are grounds for suspension/revocation proceedings under 302 KAR 50:021. Disposal methods: on-site destruction under department supervision (grinding into soil or controlled incineration), on-farm transfer to a department-authorised destroyer, or vehicle transport to a department-approved location; disposal costs incurred by the department are charged to the licence holder.

Records / USDA reporting: Licence holders must retain acquisition, production/handling, storage and disposal records for at least three (3) years and make them available to KDA (or USDA inspectors/auditors). KDA submits a Monthly Producer Report to USDA on or before the first day of each month (or next business day) with each licence's contact information and status. (302 KAR 50:046)

Total-THC measurement: For compliance, delta-9-THC concentrations are measured post-decarboxylation ("total THC"), calculated as delta-9-THC + 87.7% of delta-9-THC-acid (THC + THCa × 0.877 = total THC). (302 KAR 50:021, KDA orientation) This is the state-plan compliance measure; it is distinct from the statutory plant definition (≤0.3% delta-9 dry weight in KRS 260.850, quoted in §7.0). Compliance nuance: under 302 KAR 50:056 a result is judged against the Acceptable Hemp THC Level for the year — 0.300% delta-9-THC on a dry-weight basis plus the Measurement of Uncertainty — not against a bare 0.300% line.

7.5 CHFS hemp-derived cannabinoid product permits and registrations (902 KAR Chapter 45)

Hub page: Cabinet for Health and Family Services, Department for Public Health, Food Safety Branch, "Hemp-Derived Cannabinoid Products" — CHFS HDCP hub. The hub lists the current regulation set as: 902 KAR 45:001 (definitions), 45:012 (retail/food-service requirements), 45:021 (product registration, processing, manufacturing, storage and distribution), 45:031 (sampling/testing, laboratory requirements, remediation, COA requirements). Note: the hub page still cites "902 KAR 45:021E" for processors/manufacturers, and a 902 KAR 45:190 page still returns on the legislature site, so whether 45:190 has been superseded by the ordinary 45:021/45:012/45:031 set, and whether 45:021E has been replaced by an ordinary 45:021, remains [VERIFY] — the fees below are unaffected by that numbering question.

What CHFS distinguishes: "A Processor converts the actual hemp plant material into an isolate product. A Manufacturer uses the isolate to produce an oil, vape, gummy, drink, food product, or any edible product." (CHFS hub FAQ.) Both need a CHFS permit; the fee differs. (CHFS HDCP hub)

CHFS permit / registration Who needs it Fee Key conditions
Hemp processing permit (902 KAR 45:021 §1(1)(b)4.a) Person in Kentucky seeking to process hemp-derived cannabinoid products $3,000 Nontransferable as to person or address; posted conspicuously; renewed annually. Fee waived for facilities permitted as of 31 December 2024, payable at next annual renewal.
Hemp manufacturing permit (§1(1)(b)4.b) Person in Kentucky seeking to manufacture hemp-derived cannabinoid products (including CIB manufacturing — see §7.6) $1,000 Same nontransferable / posted / annual-renewal conditions; same 31 December 2024 waiver.
Hemp cannabinoid wholesale warehouse and distributor permit (§1(1)(b)4.c) Wholesale/distribution of hemp-derived cannabinoid products $1,000 Same conditions. CHFS hub: "All persons engaged in warehousing or distributing hemp-derived cannabinoid products in the state of Kentucky shall submit an annual registration to the Cabinet."
Hemp cosmetic permit (§1(1)(b)4.d) Hemp-derived cosmetic products $200 Same conditions. Cosmetic products are not adult-use products and may be sold to under-21s (CHFS hub).
Product registration (902 KAR 45:021 §1(5)) Each cannabinoid product or product class sold in Kentucky $200 per product or product class "A product registration fee of $200 shall be paid for each cannabinoid product or cannabinoid product class sold in Kentucky," paid to the cabinet by check or money order payable to the Kentucky State Treasurer. A new registration is required for changes in chemical composition/formula or serving size/directions. Registration requires: applicant name/address; brand/company name if different; product name; name/address of the origin of the adult-use cannabinoid product with which the final product was manufactured; complete front-and-back label copy; and a COA from an accredited third-party laboratory for the lot for each product. All fees non-refundable. CHFS decision may take up to 90 days (rejection letter, request for more information, or approval for sale/distribution). Products must be on the Approved Product Registry before retail sale; submission ≠ approval. Retailer-in-lieu registration: appears in an earlier version of 902 KAR 45:012 ("A retailer may register a product in lieu of the processor or manufacturer") — its survival in the current text is [VERIFY]; do not rely on it for a current filing.

Retail establishment / food service establishment permit — adult-use cannabinoid products (902 KAR 45:012 §1(3)) Retailers and food-service establishments offering adult-use cannabinoid products; every location must be permitted $2,000 annual permit fee per location Nontransferable as to person or address; renewed annually. Establishments registered before 31 December 2024 had the fee waived until next annual renewal. Retailers shall not be located within 1,000 feet of an elementary, middle or high school (pre-31 December 2024 registrants exempt). In-state businesses distributing/selling/serving adult-use products shall not employ anyone under 21, except a person 18+ under direct supervision of a person 21+. Products sold must be from an approved source, packaged/labelled per 902 KAR 45:021 §3, with a valid COA available on request. Adult-use products must be secured against under-21 access; proof of age required; adult-use products may not be sold/gifted/transferred to anyone under 21.

Whether already-permitted retailers also need a separate temporary-event registration is [VERIFY] against the current 45:012 text as a whole.

BUT all cannabinoid products — including non-intoxicating ones — must still be registered with the Cabinet prior to sale. Non-intoxicating cannabinoids that may be registered: CBD, CBDA, CBDV, CBDVA, CBC, CBCA, CBGA, CBG, CBN, CBT. A product with ≤2.5 mg THC per serving and a 15:1 ratio of non-intoxicating cannabinoids to THC may be sold to the general public (i.e. not treated as adult-use for the under-21 ban) [VERIFY the 2.5 mg / 15:1 threshold in the current 902 KAR 45 text]. Cosmetic products are likewise not adult-use. Adult-use cannabinoids that may be registered: delta-10-THC; delta-9-THC with ≤0.3% total THC; delta-8-THC; delta-9-THCA-A with ≤0.3% total THC; delta-9-THCV, THCVA, delta-6-THC, HHC(-), THCP, THCM; all other cannabinoids are prohibited for sale unless pre-approved by the cabinet. (902 KAR 45:021) Note: this is the pre-11 December 2026 Kentucky list; see §7.0 for the federal cliff.

Home-based processing: Prohibited. "Hemp-derived cannabinoid products shall not be manufactured, marketed, sold, or distributed by a home-based processor." (902 KAR 45:021 §2.)

7.5A Litigation over hemp-derived product rules (added — none was cited in the original slice)

Kentucky Hemp Association et al. v. Quarles et al., Boone Circuit Court, Case No. 21-CI-00836: temporary injunction 28 February 2022, and permanent injunction 3 August 2022, holding that delta-8 THC derived from compliant hemp is lawful hemp under KRS 260.850(5) so long as delta-9 THC does not exceed 0.3% on a dry-weight basis, and enjoining criminal enforcement and adverse licence action on that basis. The 2023 HB 544 committee substitute recites that 3 August 2022 permanent injunction and recites Executive Order 2022-799 (15 November 2022), directing a delta-8 regulatory structure. (HB 544 committee substitute recital) Current status of the injunction after the 902 KAR 45 regime, and after the federal cliff in §7.0, is [VERIFY against the court record] — the order was reached via a hosted copy in this audit, not via a court-record search.

7.6 ABC licences for cannabis-infused beverages (CIBs) — SB 202 (2025 Ky. Acts ch. 82)

Statute and channel: SB 202, signed 25 March 2025 (2025 Ky. Acts ch. 82). Effective 1 June 2025 for the retail-channel change: CIBs sold only at quota retail package stores, by the package, for off-premises consumption, in wet territory; bars/restaurants lost authorisation then; by-the-drink sales at fairs/festivals/events in wet territory were allowed until 1 January 2026. Potency: "shall not contain more than five (5) milligrams of intoxicating adult-use cannabinoids per twelve (12) ounce serving"; the CIB definition excludes medicinal cannabis under KRS Chapter 218B, any type of hemp tincture, and any product containing solely non-intoxicating cannabinoids. Purchasers 21+. (SB 202 record) The 5 mg state limit does not cushion the federal 0.4 mg per container cap after 11 December 2026 (see §7.0).

ABC licence What it allows Annual fee (KRS 243.030) Conditions / notes
Cannabis-infused beverage retail package licence — KRS 243.030(36) Sell CIBs by the package at retail $2,000 per annum Supplemental licence — 804 KAR 4:400's regulatory impact statement states: "Under KRS 243.403, a cannabis-infused beverage retail package license is a supplemental license to a quota retail package license." The holder must therefore also hold a quota retail package licence; the $2,000 is the CIB supplement itself, not the quota licence fee. The quota licence has its own fee under KRS 243.030 (amount not retrieved in this audit — do not guess; [VERIFY against the current KRS 243.030 fee list]). The impact statement notes the number of quota retail package licences able to be issued is 1,888 — that is the ceiling on businesses that could hold a CIB retail licence, not a count of CIB licensees. Holder shall not apply for or hold the incompatible licence listed in KRS 243.030(5) or KRS 243.040(3) (KRS 243.110(4)(a)). Wet-territory requirement applies. Gas stations, convenience stores and smoke shops cannot sell CIBs.
Cannabis-infused beverage distributor's licence — KRS 243.030(37) Distribute CIBs wholesale $1,000 per annum May be held as a primary licence or as a supplemental licence to a distributor's or wholesaler's licence; the supplemental distributor's licence is also $1,000 per annum (KRS 243.030(38)). ABC estimated (804 KAR 4:400) fewer than 100 businesses would seek a distributor's licence (an estimate, not a count).
Direct shipper Type B licence — KRS 243.030(39) Ship CIBs directly to consumers (the DTC exception to the three-tier rule) $1,000 per annum
CIB manufacturer licence (ABC) Manufacture CIBs No standalone ABC manufacturer fee — confirmed as absent from KRS 243.030 KRS 243.027 frames the manufacturer as licensed by the Department for Public Health (i.e. the CHFS hemp manufacturing permit in §7.5, $1,000, plus product registration). ABC's role is distributor/retail/direct-shipper licensing. A DPH-approved CIB manufacturer may also self-distribute CIBs in the same manner as distilled spirits and ship under a direct shipper licence (KRS 243.401(4)). Do not publish an ABC manufacturer fee.

Application fee (all ABC licences in KRS 243.030): A nonrefundable application fee of fifty dollars ($50) is charged to process each new application under KRS 243.030, except for subsections (4), (8), (9), (10), (12), (15), (19), and (20). "The application fee shall be applied to the licensing fee if the license is issued; otherwise it shall be retained by the department." It is therefore credited against the licence fee if issued, not additional on top. (Citation correction: this is the unnumbered paragraph at the end of KRS 243.030, after subsection (42) — not subsection (40), which is the $60 transitional-licence processing fee under KRS 243.045. The 804 KAR 4:400 impact statement's "$50 offset" sentence is this provision.)

CIB taxes (added row): Excise tax of $1.92 per gallon on the use, sale, or distribution of cannabis-infused beverages (proportional per gallon for other container sizes), effective 1 July 2025 (KRS 243.720(4)), plus an 11% wholesale sales tax (KRS 243.884) on CIB sales by manufacturers that direct-ship or self-distribute and by wholesalers distributing CIBs, with monthly reports due by the 20th of the following month. (Department of Revenue, Alcohol Taxes) Chapter note: KRS 243.720 was amended by 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 98 §20 — a separate revenue act, not SB 202 (ch. 82); the two chapter numbers are not in conflict.

Application mechanics (ABC): Under 804 KAR 4:400, an applicant for an alcoholic-beverage or cannabis-infused-beverage licence completes the New License Application at the online portal (ABC portal); renewals under KRS 243.090 and 804 KAR 4:390 are also via the portal; transfers of 10% or more ownership interest, and transfers to different premises, require department approval via the portal.

Transition (post-Run 1, dated July 2026): The 804 KAR 4:400 impact statement (amendment) states the regulation "will affect all businesses seeking to continue selling cannabis-infused beverages at retail or wholesale after July 1, 2026" and that businesses selling CIBs under a DPH permit "who desire to continue to sell cannabis-infused beverages as such when, after July 1, 2026 those permits expire, will need to apply for a cannabis-infused beverage retail package license or a cannabis-infused beverage distributor's license, respectively, and pay the statutory application and license fees." In other words, the DPH-permit channel for CIB retail/wholesale expired after 1 July 2026 and the ABC licence channel is now the operative one. Practical consequence: a CIB retailer in late 2026 needs the ABC CIB retail package licence (+ quota licence), not merely the CHFS retailer permit that sufficed in the interim period — but CIB manufacturing and product registration remain CHFS/DPH. [VERIFY on the live ABC portal: whether the CIB retail package licence application is live on the portal as of October 2026, and whether any DPH CIB retail permits were extended past 1 July 2026.]

Pending proposal — not law: 2026 HB 896 (introduced 4 March 2026, referred to House Licensing, Occupations & Administrative Regulations 11 March 2026) would amend KRS 243.030 to reduce the CIB retail package fee from $2,000 to $500. That explains the $500 figure in earlier passes; it is NOT current law. Current law remains $2,000. Do not cite $500 (or $520) as a current fee.

ABC licence counts / lists: No public ABC CIB licensee list or count was located. No ABC CIB licence total is stated. The 1,888 figure is a quota ceiling, not a licensee count; the "<100 distributor" figure is an ABC estimate, not a count.
